title_original: Champions League manager immediately resigns minutes after opening match
body_original: Fenerbahce manager Ismail Kartal announced that he has resigned moments after his side’s Champions League opener. Kartal, who was only appointed in June, confirmed he would be leaving in his post-match press conference. Kartal quit his job just minutes after the full time whistle in the Champions League Getty The Turkish giants had just drawn at home to Roma in their first match of the league phase when he revealed the news. “I am resigning from my position while there is still time,” he said. “I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return. “I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players… our president and managers tried to help us in every way. Those were wonderful days. “As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning from my position. “Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today. “I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team.” Kartal has now ended his fourth spell in charge of Fenerbahce, having taken charge in 2014, 2022, 2023 and earlier this year. During his fourth spell, he only led the club into 11 games, winning six of them, drawing three and losing two, with one of the wins coming against Lyon last month, which ended in a chaotic brawl . Fenerbahce’s two losses had both come in the Turkish Super Lig though, meaning they are sitting ninth after four games. And now, after failing to win in the Champions League , the 65-year-old has made the decision to depart. Kartal revealed that he and the team have decided that he will leave his post Getty Player stunned by Kartal resignation It appears Kartal didn’t run this by his players with Fenerbahce goalscorer Archie Brown discovering the news while giving interviews to journalists post-match. The English left-back cut a stunned figure when a Fenerbahce official revealed to him that Kartal had resigned, asking: “What do you mean he resigned?” After it was explained Kartal announced his resignation in a press conference, a confused Brown enquired: “As what? As coach?” Wondering if things had been lost in translation, Brown asked: “What do you mean, resigned? He’s not the coach any more?” Resigned to the news of Kartal resigning was true, a shell-shocked Brown finished by saying: “I didn’t know about this.” View Tweet: https://t.co/Iq8hZO7pDE Leaving with a point Kartal dropped the bombshell news straight after his side drew 1-1 with Serie A side Roma in Istanbul. Bryan Cristante scored the opener for the visitors in the 39th minute, with them taking their lead into half time. But Birmingham-born Brown equalised just after the break and neither side could then find a winner. Fenerbahce’s line-up included six-time Premier League winners with Manchester City Ederson and Nathan Ake, World Cup winner N’Golo Kante and ex- Manchester United winger Mason Greenwood. Romelu Lukaku was also introduced as a late substitute, but he was unable to find the winning goal for his side. Fenerbahce will now be looking to bring in a new boss ahead of their league game against Gaziantep on Sunday evening. Their next European outing sees them travel to Aston Villa on October 14. Fenerbahce host Liverpool later in the league phase on November 4.

title_original: Anthony Gordon hands Barcelona unexpected boost worth millions after just five games for the club
body_original: Barcelona have already received huge value from signing Anthony Gordon just five matches into his career at the Nou Camp. When it was announced in May that football royalty Barcelona had agreed a £69.3million deal with Newcastle United for Gordon , more than a few eyebrows were raised. But the Englishman has quickly silenced any doubters by getting off to a stellar start with his new club, and this has been reflected in the impressive rise in his transfer value since the move. READ MORE: Barcelona make huge Anthony Gordon transfer move after 'not normal' debut in Champions League Anthony Gordon's transfer value soars after stellar start with Barcelona Ahead of Gordon's move, it was widely believed that Barcelona would instead sign Marcus Rashford as their new left winger, following the Manchester United star's relatively successful loan spell at the Nou Camp last season. Rashford's loan deal included a clause that would have allowed Barcelona to make the move permanent €30 million (£35m), but they instead paid nearly double to sign his England teammate, Gordon. Despite some initial scepticism from fans, it seems that this decision has immediately paid off, with Gordon providing five assists in his first four La Liga appearances ahead of making his Champions League debut for the club as a second-half substitute in a 5-1 win over Feyenoord. Gordon's fiery start with Barcelona has not only ingratiated him with fans but also increased his value by as much as £8m in only a matter of months. According to CIES Football Observatory's latest valuation of the England international, the 25-year-old is now estimated to be worth around €90million (£77.3m). Of course, if Gordon continues to perform as he has been in his first weeks with Barcelona, it stands to reason that this value will only continue to rise over the course of the 2026/27 season and beyond. And after Barcelona tied him down to a five-year contract, the Spanish giants have plenty of time to extract the maximum value out of Gordon in the coming years. READ MORE: Marcus Rashford receives explanation from Barcelona over decision to snub him for Anthony Gordon Hansi Flick reveals the one thing Anthony Gordon must improve to succeed at Barcelona Although it's safe to say that Barcelona boss Flick has been impressed with Gordon's start this season, it doesn't mean that he's been completely flawless in his opening games for the club. During the crucial win over Feyenoord in the Champions League, the winger had plenty of opportunities to score his first goal for his new club, but ultimately failed to contribute to either of the two goals scored since he was introduced. "I think as a striker, from his side, you want to score goals," Flick said post-match. "He has had some chances and he missed them. But he has made the final pass to prepare the goals and this is also very important." But, with Barcelona currently sitting top of La Liga, two points ahead of second-placed Alaves, and three points above historic rivals Real Madrid in third, it's likely Flick won't be too harsh on Gordon for not putting away his chances just yet. title_original: What would actually happen if Chelsea were stripped of 2017 Premier League title after Mauricio Pochettino demand
body_original: Mauricio Pochettino recently called for Chelsea to be stripped of their 2016-17 Premier League title, and precedent does exist for Tottenham Hotspur to receive the trophy belatedly. Pochettino, who coached both Chelsea and Spurs prior to his appointment with the USMNT, has called for the Blues to be stripped of their 2016-17 Premier League title, which they won with 93 points. That title arrived under Antonio Conte, with Poch’s Spurs in second on 86 points. If Chelsea were to be stripped of their crown, precedent does exist for the North London club to receive it — but that outcome is far from certain. READ NEXT: Dejan Kulusevski return update given after 477 days out with specific games set as target Could Tottenham actually be awarded Chelsea's 2017 Premier League title? Pochettino recently claimed that Tottenham Hotspur “didn’t compete with the same rules” as Chelsea , after the Blues admitted to making £47 million in undisclosed payments between 2011 and 2018. However, it remains unlikely that Spurs will receive a redistributed Premier League trophy, as the case against Chelsea to be stripped of their title is weak. At the time, the Premier League did not impose a sporting sanction on Chelsea, rather their punishment was enforced financially, and through transfer bans. In July, the club was fined £10 million, and given a suspended two-window transfer ban, for breaching rules related to agent payments between 2009 and 2022. The English top-flight recalculated Chelsea’s accounts from the time, and determined that the undisclosed payments in question would not have caused a PSR breach. And while the now-concluded disciplinary decision could be reopened, it remains unlikely, with Chelsea’s punishments having already been imposed. And if the Blues were stripped of their title, there is no guarantee that Tottenham Hotspur would automatically inherit the Premier League trophy — precedent exists in both their favour, and against it. READ NEXT: 'That is criminal!' - Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer derail live Sky Sports interview after chaotic Leeds game What happened when football titles have previously been stripped from clubs? The precedent in question was established in the Italian top-flight, as Serie A titles were stripped from Juventus in 2004-05 and 2005-06 amid doping allegations. That scandal, an infamously dark moment in Italian football history, spiralled from doping accusations, to an investigation into match-fixing agreements held between Juventus staff and Serie A officials. Among the offences were Juventus match-assigned referees being favourable to the Serie A champions, pressuring officials to make decisions that benefited the Old Lady, and issuing punishments that rendered opposition players unable to face Fabio Capello’s side. As a result, Juventus were stripped of two successive Serie A titles, but the decisions did not align. For 2004-05, the trophy remained unassigned, while in 2005-06, the honour was redistributed to Inter. Therefore, the Serie A’s established precedent makes it unclear as to whether Spurs would see the Premier League trophy passed to them from Chelsea — the likelihood being a coin flip. Pochettino believes any outcome barring Tottenham Hotspur receiving the title would be incorrect, stating: “We should win one title, one Premier League. We should have been awarded it. "[Chelsea] were punished, they admitted, so that's it? The title should be for the team that was second. It's not me complaining. It's the truth. If they admitted they broke the rules, the Premier League title was for the second best team. "I'm not scared to say the truth. The Chelsea fans will be upset with me because I'm saying this, but if we were at Tottenham and broke the rules I'd admit the same,” concluded the 54-year-old. READ NEXT: Chelsea star banished from first-team at Stamford Bridge in brutal Xabi Alonso call Time will tell whether Pochettino’s wish will come true, but even if Chelsea’s case was to be re-opened, Spurs receiving the 2016-17 Premier League title is anything but a certainty.

title_original: 'That is criminal!' - Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer derail live Sky Sports interview after chaotic Leeds game
body_original: Morgan Rogers was furious when he was snubbed for the man-of-the-match award after Chelsea's comeback win over Leeds United in the Carabao Cup. On Wednesday night, Leeds United looked set to pull off a major upset as they took a two-goal lead over Chelsea in their Carabao Cup third-round clash at Stamford Bridge. Unfortunately for the northern team, a spectacular second-half performance from Xabi Alonso's side saw Leeds lose 6-2, largely thanks to star summer signing Rogers. READ MORE: Chelsea star banished from first-team at Stamford Bridge in brutal Xabi Alonso call Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer argue over Leeds man-of-the-match award With Chelsea trailing 1-0 at half-time, Alonso brought Rogers, Cole Palmer and Pedro Neto on to completely transform the game. Shortly after their introduction, Palmer scored twice, a penalty in the 53rd minute before scoring a tidy goal just two minutes later, with Rogers assisting four of the six Chelsea goals. Therefore, when it was revealed that Palmer had been named the man of the match, Rogers was fuming, leading to a hilarious exchange between the pair. "Mate, I got four assists! Nah, nah, I can't believe that. That is mental. He scored a penalty. That is mental," Rogers shouted. Then Palmer, staying humble, said: "I started the comeback, but I’ll shout you out and say you should’ve had it, don’t worry about that.” To which Rogers replied: "Don't mention me. I am just a bystander. That is criminal." According to Opta, Rogers technically only got three assists, but it's more than fair to say that he absolutely deserved the award following his fundamental role in Chelsea's stunning comeback victory. "Mate, I got four assists!" "That is criminal!" Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer arguing over the POTM award! 🤣 pic.twitter.com/X2PkPnSGDk — Sky Sports Football (@SkyFootball) September 9, 2026 Inside Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers stunning start to the season When Rogers arrived at Stamford Bridge as the British Premier League transfer record for a massive £117million, expectations were high on the Englishman to perform well in his first season with Chelsea. And that's exactly what he's done, picking up two goals and four assists across his first five appearances for his new club in the Premier League and Carabao Cup. Paramount to this success has been his close relationship with Palmer, who he has been friends with since their time together at the Manchester City academy and England youth teams. Like Rogers, Palmer has enjoyed a stellar start to the season, clearly putting his omission from England's World Cup squad over the summer behind him. In Chelsea's five matches so far this summer, he's scored four goals and assisted one, reminding fans why he's one of the best players in the league. It therefore comes as no surprise that both Palmer and Rogers, alongside teammate Joao Pedro, are among the most transferred-in players in Fantasy Premier League ahead of their next match against newly-promoted Hull City. However, it's possible that FPL managers looking for a big haul from the Chelsea lads this weekend could be surprised for one key reason. title_original: Michael Olise divides football fans with uncomfortable interview after Bayern Munich win in Champions League
body_original: Michael Olise has left football fans with an awkward interview after bagging a brace in Bayern Munich's first Champions League game of the season. Vincent Kompany' s side trounced Bodo/Glimt 5-0 at the Allianz Arena, with all of the goals coming in the second half. Jamal Musiala broke the deadlock in the 47th minute, before Harry Kane and Alphonso Davies got in on the act. Olise added gloss on the win with a late double, which puts Bayern second in the overall league table after one game. Michael Olise goes viral for brief interview answers after Man of the Match display The Frenchman, one of the most in-form players in world football at the moment, was interviewed by DAZN following the win. But Olise, a man of few words, prompted reaction aplenty with the way in which he answered questions. The interviewer praised his shooting ability and asked how it felt to score two brilliant goals, to which the Man of the Match replied: "I don't know". READ NEXT: Michael Olise has played entire footballing career without signing contract that 'doesn't interest him' He was asked whether it is something he thinks about or just does, with Olise commenting, "I shoot and it goes in or doesn't go in". The presenter then made the point that if it is easy, everyone could do it as he said Olise was "the only one". Laughing awkwardly, he said: "I'm not the only one who can score goals. I don't think so". 🚨😅| Michael Olise asked how it feels to score such great goals: "I don't know". Asked how he does it: "I shoot and it goes in" pic.twitter.com/vw5b7ojCdI — Kalshi FC (@KalshiFC) September 10, 2026 The former Crystal Palace winger's demeanour and short responses led to the journalist telling Olise that he "makes it quite difficult to do an interview". The 24-year-old clearly prefers being on the pitch to being in interviews and naturally, his chat went viral. One fan did not enjoy Olise's interview, writing on X: "Cannot be real adults laughing at this. Just comes across awfully, grown man putting on this act is beyond cringe." A second said: "It's not funny and it shouldn't be normalised either. This kind of response is directly disrespectful to the journalist whose sole intention was to empathize with their interviewee. A third added: "Now this is awful this is not nonchalant matter." Another user had a different view, commenting: "I love this guy. He just wanna do his bob and go home." A final person agreed and said: "Straight to the point man I love it." Why Michael Olise rarely celebrates goals in an emotional manner explained Olise is a unique character known for being incredible nonchalant and laidback and it even extends to his goal celebrations as well as interviews. Often he will be muted even after curling one in the top corner. It dates back to his time playing for Reading, with Michael Morrison explaining it is not something he started doing when he got more popular. "We’d say he’s a bit weird sometimes because when he scored goals, he sometimes wouldn’t celebrate," he told The Athletic . "We’d be like, ‘Mike, you’ve just scored an important goal and you’re just walking back?’. What’s he doing? "Then he’d play two-touch with the manager in the gym, he’d win a point in that, and he’d be shouting and celebrating, but on a Saturday, he’d score a goal in front of the home end and just stand there. "We never really worked out why. He could never give us an answer but he’s just different; a special player." Olise was asked the question during an interview with Highsnobiety in June and explained that he just doesn't get the same feeling as other players when he finds the net. He said: "I am not a super emotional person. I don’t react the same way everyone else reacts."

title_original: Archie Brown finds out during post-match interview that Fenerbahce manager Ismail Kartal has resigned
body_original: Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown was visibly stunned after being told that manager Ismail Kartal had announced his resignation following the club's Champions League clash against Roma. Kartal, who was appointed Fenerbahce boss in June this year, announced his sudden resignation to the press on Thursday evening, shortly after the Turkish side recorded a 1-1 draw in Istanbul. Speaking to reporters, he said as per GZT : "Throughout the season, during the training camps we held with our players, our president and managers tried to help us. Those were wonderful days. "As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning. I thank the press, the fans, and my fellow players who have supported me until today." "I have left my post tonight," added Kartal. "I made this decision to pave the way for my club. I have decided to resign from my position. I will never return. Good evening to everyone." Moments later, goalscorer Archie Brown was conducting his post-match interview alongside an interpreter when news filtered through about Kartal's unexpected decision. Brown was asked the following question by a reporter: "Ismail Kartal resigned from his position. Did he speak with you?" Archie Brown was taken aback by the news. Image credit: Dunyanin With a puzzled look on his face, a confused Brown turned to his interpreter and asked: "What do you mean he resigned? He's not the coach anymore? He said this just now? I didn't know about this." You can see footage of that moment below. Archie Brown finding out Ismail Kartal (Fenerbahçe manager) has resigned post game by u/u8kay in soccer After taking charge of Fenerbahce for the fourth time this summer following previous spells in 2014, 2022 and 2023, Kartal walks away with a mixed record on his CV. He led the Turkish giants to six wins, three draws and two defeats across his 11 games in charge, but pressure mounted after those losses came in the Super Lig. As a result, they sit ninth in the table. Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi hit with UEFA bans after "offensive gesture" On the subject of Fenerbahce, Mason Greenwood and Matteo Guendouzi have both been punished by UEFA for "offensive gestures" that were made during their heated Champions League win over Lyon. Last month, Fenerbahce beat Lyon 3-2 on aggregate in the play-off to qualify for the competition's league phase following goals but there was huge controversy at the final whistle . Being a former Marseille player, Guendouzi was jeered throughout the game and his emotions got the better of him as he appeared to taunt the supporters. He was seen shouting "Allez l'OM" to the camera as he showed his allegiance to Marseille and followed up by flipping off the fans. Mason Greenwood, who joined Fenerbahce from Marseille this summer, was also present and subject to the UEFA investigation. The former Manchester United forward was given a one-match suspended ban which is "subject to a probationary period of one year", on top of a £26,000 fine, for "violating the basic rules of decent conduct".

title_original: FPL expert builds perfect wildcard team for GW4 that will help every manager climb their mini league
body_original: I've finished in the top 0.02% of all FPL teams for the past two seasons, and this is the team I would put together if I was wildcarding this week. We're just three gameweeks into the 2026/27 Premier League season, and many Fantasy Premier League (FPL) managers are already making use In Gameweek Three, a record-breaking number of managers used their triple captain chip, mostly for Erling Haaland's nine-pointer against Coventry City, while others used their Free Hits. For this week, three weeks of fixtures and data give FPL managers a great chance to reflect on the start of the season and build a whole new team with their wildcard chip. Of course, the question then becomes: who should you pick on your wildcard this week? Well, I finished 32nd overall in the 2024/25 season and 1,940th in 2025/26, and this is the team I'd be putting together if my wildcard was active in Gameweek four. READ MORE: FPL managers are making a major mistake ahead of Gameweek four as more than five MILLION fall into trap The BEST FPL Gameweek Four draft Three gameweeks in, we know which of the popular players are, and aren't performing well, and which teams are worth targeting in the coming weeks. For example, everybody expected Chelsea to improve under Xabi Alonso, but not many would have expected them to be quite as good as they have been in their opening fixtures. Meanwhile, while expectations were low for Coventry City, conceding five goals and failing to score even one in three matches is far worse than we had anticipated. With all that in mind, here's my wildcard draft for FPL Gameweek Four. GK - Bart Verbruggen (BHA, £4.5m) Starting at the back, I think a £4.5m goalkeeper is still the best way forward, despite David Raya (ARS, £6.0m) being a tempting option. Of the £4.5m options, I think Brighton keeper Verbruggen is still the best, with the Seagulls performing well enough in their opening matches, with one clean sheet from three. Admittedly, after a promising fixture away to Coventry City this week, the upcoming run of ARS (H), SUN (A), CRY (H), LIV (A) and MCI (A) isn't the best, but I still prefer him to the popular Antonin Kinsky at Spurs. DEF - Riccardo Calafiori (ARS, £5.7m) One of the most obvious picks on this list is Calafiori, who has started the season as by far the best defender in the game. Other than the mighty Hull City defenders, who have amazingly kept three clean sheets in three, Calafiori is the next highest-scoring defender in the game so far, with 22 points from his opening three matches. Two clean sheets, two assists and two bonus points in three matches as a nailed starter for the best defensive team in the league, he's a no-brainer on wildcard. DEF - Ezri Konsa (ARS, £4.4m) Speaking of no-brainers, an Arsenal double-up with Konsa available at just £4.4m is the easiest decision you can make in your wildcard draft. Konsa was priced at £4.5m at the start of the season, when he was still playing for Aston Villa, but dropped when people who started the season with him sold him when he wasn't playing. But it now looks like the Englishman has a nailed-on spot in Mikel Arteta's defence, at least while William Saliba is out, so for now, he simply has to be in your team at this price. Konsa could now be the best value player in FPL since his move to Arsenal. (Image: Getty) DEF - Malick Thiaw (NEW, £5.0m) Completing the starting lineup of defenders, I think Thiaw at Newcastle could be a bargain at £5.0m. Newcastle haven't had the easiest of starts to the season and yet the German has managed eight points from three matches, thanks to a clean sheet and defensive contribution points. Yes, he scored an own goal last week against Bournemouth, but don't let that put you off with LEE (A), HUL (H) and COV (A) in his next three. MID - Bruno Fernandes (MUN, £12.0m) Another easy pick on the wildcard is Man United captain Fernandes, who has more than lived up to his 12m price tag so far this season. With 27 points, he's the second highest-scoring midfielder in the game right now, behind only Cody Gakpo, and despite his price, it's hard to look past him. He can pick up goals, assists, bonus, defensive contribution points and clean sheet points even in the harder fixtures, so just get him in your team. MID - Cole Palmer (CHE, £9.6m) Palmer will probably be one of the most popular picks for managers making transfers, either using their wildcard or not, in Gameweek Four ahead of Hull City at home. After Thomas Tuchel left him out of England's World Cup squad over the summer, Palmer has come back with two goals and one assist in Chelsea's three Premier League fixtures so far. Chelsea's fixtures look pretty decent in the near future and, like Fernandes, Palmer is able to score points in several ways, so much so that he'd even be my captaincy pick for Gameweek Four. MID - Enzo Fernandez (MCI, £6.9m) Not to spoil the rest of the team, but this wildcard leaves managers with a £100m budget with 0.1m remaining at the time of writing. Many would use this spare cash to take Liverpool's Dominik Szoboszlai (£7.0m) over my pick, Fernandez at £6.9m, but I've been really impressed with City's new top signing. Other than Haaland, it's hard to pick a City attacker that's even close to being nailed, but Fernandez's transfer fee, form and close relationship with manager Enzo Maresca means he's probably one of the safer picks. And speaking of Haaland , Fernandez seems to be gelling well with City's star man, providing an assist in the Champions League win over Porto and another for Haaland's second (disallowed) goal against Coventry. He's just 3.2% owned right now, so I think a punt on Fernandez is a great shout for managers who have activated their wildcard. Fernandez could be a great punt for FPL managers using their wildcard. (Image: Getty) MID - Pascal Gross (BHA, £5.6m) Gross keeps his place as the best budget-friendly midfielder in my wildcard draft, despite the emergence of Mamadou Sangare (£5.7m) at Brentford. Like Verbruggen, the Brighton talisman has a nice fixture against Coventry up next ahead of some tough games on the horizon, but with a goal and an assist against Chelsea in Gameweek Two, he's shown he can show up any week. Many will still go for Sangare at this price point, but with BOU (A), CHE (H), AVL (A), LIV (H) in his next four, don't be surprised if the Brentford superstar is sold en masse in the coming weeks and drops in price. FWD - Erling Haaland (MCI, £15.5m) Back to the no-brainers now, Haaland simply has to be in your FPL teams, probably for the remainder of the season. Although some may have expected more, three goals in three is still enough to justify Haaland's place in your team and at this stage of the season, going against a player who is owned by 71.3% of managers is just silly. FWD - Joao Pedro (CHE, £7.7m) Another in-form player who will be brought into plenty of teams for Gameweek Four thanks to the upcoming meeting with Hull City. When he started the season at £7.5m, Pedro looked to be one of the biggest bargains and the game and despite two price rises already, that's still the case. With two goals, two assists and 21 points, the Chelsea striker is too good to pass up on, especially given the lack of standout options up front so far this season. FWD - Thierno Barry (EVE, £5.6m) Barry is another punt in the wildcard draft, going against the much more popular Dominic Calvert-Lewin (£6.0m), who is in nearly a quarter of teams. Comparatively, Barry is in just 5.6% of teams currently, presenting another chance to make the most of your wildcard and take a punt on a player with huge upside. TOT (A), IPS (H) and HUL (A) are next up for Everton and Barry's place up front is absolutely nailed-on, so there's plenty of chances of a haul in the coming weeks. Admittedly, after this run of three matches I'd be looking at moving Barry on ahead of CHE (H), ARS (A) and NEW (A), but at that point you can hope his work for your team would be already done. READ MORE: Millions of FPL managers are making major mistake with three transfers ahead of GW4 BENCH - Dan Bentley (GK, COV, 4.0m) Tarik Muharemovic (DEF, LEE, £5.0m), John Egan (DEF, HUL, £4.1m), Regan Slater (MID, HUL, £4.5m) Rounding up the team is the bench. Don't worry about picking Bentley specifically, any £4m goalkeeper that's not highly owned, so you avoid any potential price drops, and not from a team you're likely to want to triple up at some point this season. Muharemovic is another £5m defender that I really like the look of due to his defensive contributions so far this season, with the new Leeds signing scoring 14 points despite only one clean sheet thanks to his defensive actions. The Leeds defender came close to hitting the defensive contribution threshold in his first game and comfortably surpassed it in the following two gameweeks, so we can expect him to keep that up in the coming weeks, despite some mixed fixtures. While we're discussing defensive contribution magnets, Egan has also smashed the threshold in two of his three fixtures and, while we shouldn't expect Hull's clean sheet streak to continue, we can expect Egan to keep netting some defensive contribution points. Meanwhile, his Hull teammate Regan Slater rounds up the bench as a nailed-on starter at £4.5m who can chip in with the occasional goal contribution.

title_original: Mikel Arteta responds to Arsenal star who claims he was mistreated during summer exit
body_original: Arteta was shocked by comments made by Gabriel Jesus (Picture: Getty) Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has hit back at Gabriel Jesus after claims he was mistreated during his final weeks at the club. Jesus, a £45million signing from Manchester City in 2022, left the Gunners this summer, sealing a permanent move to Barcelona. In a recent interview, the Brazil international claimed he was ordered to train away from the Arsenal first-team before his exit and was kept in the dark over his situation. ‘I did all the pre-season with Arsenal [normally],’ Jesus said. ‘Obviously I knew already that probably I would not play there or get some opportunity, but no one told me anything. Sign up for In The Mixer, Metro's football newsletter Get exclusive analysis and previews of the biggest games every Friday. Sign up now for free. ‘I was training with the group, and then, from nothing, they put me to train apart from the group.’ Those comments came after Arsenal legend Ian Wright questioned the club’s treatment of Gabriel Martinelli , who was sold to Al-Hilal this month. The Brazilian, who joined the club as an 18-year-old seven years ago, was left of matchday squads while his future was being resolved. ‘It really makes me feel uncomfortable,’ Wright said. ‘I think he’s done enough with this team, with this squad, to be treated with a little bit more respect than he’s being treated at the moment.’ Jesus joined Barcelona this summer (Picture: Shutterstock Editorial) Speaking in a press conference on Friday, Arteta was quizzed on both sets of comments. He told reporters: ‘Very surprised, to be fair, especially because with Gabi [Jesus] I had an individual talk in the dressing room. I don’t know what words were said, it is fine. ‘The words we used for each other, it was all about gratitude. I don’t know, it is okay. Sometimes I understand when you have to deliver bad news or news that people don’t expect, those things [you can] react [to].’ Martinelli left Arsenal after seven years (Picture: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire) Arteta admitted it was up to him to be ‘bad cop’ but also pointed out Leandro Trossard ’s return to the club last weekend to watch the victory over Chelsea, two months on from leaving to join Besiktas. ‘Somebody has to be the bad cop. If I have to be, I have to be and I understand. ‘What is important is normally what happens three months later, six months later, when Trossard comes in, he is the dressing room with us, the atmosphere and the relationship you have. ‘Things got so far with other players that they left, at some point the relationship has been really good. I hope that is the same case.’ Comment now Comments Add Metro as a Preferred Source on Google Add as preferred source

title_original: Darren Fletcher involved in heated exchange with Man United fans after Sabah win
body_original: Darren Fletcher was involved in heated exchange with a Manchester United fan after the 4-0 win over Sabah on Thursday night. United returned to the Champions League in style after a two-season absence, with Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Benjamin Sesko and Lisandro Martinez all on target. But in a bizarre turn of events, United legend Fletcher was forced to put a United supporter in his place in footage which emerged from outside of Old Trafford. @StrettyEnd_official on Instagram shared the clip, where Under-18s coach Fletcher was seen having a go at a supporter. Why Darren Fletcher put Man United fan in his place after Sabah win It was claimed the issue was over players refusing to sign autographs for supporters outside the ground. Fletcher was not happy with one fan's "abusive" tone and told him straight in front of people who had gathered outside, including the Sabah players. READ MORE: Darren Fletcher hits out at FA after seeing how they handled Youth Cup final between Man Utd and Man City In the video, Fletcher was heard saying: "Listen, it doesn't matter you can't speak like that, have some respect. You're the reason that people don't sign." His comments were met with huge cheers from other fans, who chanted his name as he walked away. Fletcher, who had a short spell as interim boss last season, was watching one of his sons, Tyler, who was on the bench for the win against Sabah. View this post on Instagram On social media, fans were split about Fletcher's outburst. One supporter on Instagram disagreed with what he said and commented, "Fan is right the players should acknowledge and do their bits pre and post match. Fergie would expect that. Another example of how standards have dropped." A second added: "The fan is right though." A third stated: "I’m a Liverpool fan and must admit this is brilliant from fletcher. He is spot on." A fourth user wrote: "The self entitlement of fans is laughable. You’ve bought a ticket to watch the match. If you get anything else on top of that it’s a bonus." READ NEXT: Lisandro Martinez gets round of applause from CBS studio for response to 'who is your favourite pundit on the show' Man United had strict autograph rule enforced by Ruben Amorim The issue surrounding whether players should be stopping to sign for fans outside the stadiums is one that clearly divides opinions, but Ruben Amorim's view on the matter was very clear. The former United boss, who preceded both Fletcher and Michael Carrick, brought in a strict rule regarding autographs. According to The Athletic , Amorim demanded that half of the squad must sign autographs before a game at Old Trafford, with the remaining half obliged to sign afterwards. Having time for the supporters was a basic principle enforced by Sir Alex Ferguson, United's greatest ever manager. United are back at Old Trafford on Sunday, hosting Manchester City in the first derby of the season.

title_original: Lisandro Martinez gets round of applause from CBS studio for response to 'who is your favourite pundit on the show'
body_original: Micah Richards asked Manchester United's Lisandro Martínez to name his favourite member of the CBS Sports punditry team - and his "I like to watch quality players" response is going viral. United began their Champions League campaign with victory over Azerbaijan Premier League side Sabah on Thursday as goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes, Benjamin Sesko and Martinez sealed a 4-0 win. It was an evening to remember for Martinez , whose effort against Sabah was his first-ever goal at Old Trafford. READ MORE: Why Bryan Mbeumo, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro are wearing different kits to Man Utd teammates vs Sabah After the full-time whistle, the Argentine was in great spirits. In fact, during his post-match interview with CBS , he gave an entertaining response when Micah Richards asked his trademark "who is your favourite on the show" question. It didn't take long for Martinez to reveal his admiration for former Arsenal striker Thierry Henry , a reply that didn't go down well with Richards and Jamie Carragher, with the latter saying: "What about us defenders?" Without much hesitation, Martinez responded by saying: "I like to watch quality players." Martinez was given a round of applause from Henry, Carragher and Richards. Image credit: CBS In the interview, Richards also asked Martinez if he used to watch Carragher and what he thought of the former Liverpool defender, who has been one of Martinez's most vocal critics in the past. The Argentine once again left the studio in stitches, replying: "As a player? Good person." Jamie Carragher previously admitted he was wrong about Lisandro Martinez Initially, an unconvinced Carragher was critical of United's £56.7 million move for Martinez. Speaking after United had lost their first two games of the Premier League season against Brighton and Brentford in 2022, Carragher questioned whether the defender would be able to play in a back four because of his relatively short height, 5ft 9in. “We should never judge managers or players too early, but I'm convinced this can't work because the size of him playing in a back four," Carragher said on Sky Sports. "Maybe he could go left-back, maybe he could play in a back three, but in a back four, he cannot play there in the Premier League." Martinez would go on to become one of United's standout performers across the season, and in May 2023, Carragher issued an apology on Sky for his previous comments. “He (Martinez) is a warrior and a leader," said Carragher. "He and Casemiro are the two new signings who have transformed Man Utd. So apologies to Lisandro Martinez and Man United fans, you can stop tweeting me now about it."

title_original: Mauricio Pochettino demands Premier League strip club of title in extraordinary interview
body_original: Mauricio Pochettino has called for his former club Chelsea to be stripped of a Premier League title in a new bombshell interview. Pochettino had one season in charge at Chelsea in the 2023/24 season, before he left via a mutual agreement following a sixth-placed finish. But his best work in England came with Spurs , who he led to consecutive second-placed finishes in the 2015/16 and 2016/17 campaigns. Spurs recorded 86 points but lost out to Antonio Conte Chelsea's, who recovered from a shaky start to win the title by seven points. Mauricio Pochettino calls out Chelsea rule breaches in extraordinary interview However, nearly a decade on and Pochettino has claimed he should be a Premier League champion as he spoke out about Chelsea being punished. In March, Chelsea, having been charged by the Premier League for breaches of competition rules, were hit with a £10.75 million fine. The fine would have been £20 million but was reduced by 50% because Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital self-reported 74 breaches of Football Association rules when they bought Chelsea in 2022. A six points deduction was not applied upon appeal after Chelsea admitted to making £47 million in secret payments to unregistered agents and third-parties regarding transfers between 2011 and 2018. Transfers involving Eden Hazard, Samuel Eto'o, Willian, Ramires, David Luiz, Andre Schurrle and Nemanja Matic were in the Premier League's report and all four of those aforementioned players played in Chelsea's title triumph. None of the players are implicated or accused of any wrongdoing. Speaking to UK media outlets, including the BBC , Pochettino said: "We should win one title, one Premier League. We should have been awarded it. "They were punished, they admitted, so that's it? The title should be for the team that was second. "It's true that we didn't compete with the same rules. OK, now we can say that they scored goals, they won games, and like this. OK, that's it, but it's completely fair to say that we didn't compete before the start of the season with the same card. "Maybe with the same rules, if we apply the same things, maybe we could've signed some players that would have made the team better or scored more goals. It's not me complaining. It's the truth. If they admitted they broke the rules, the Premier League title was for the second best team. "I'm not scared to say the truth. The Chelsea fans will be upset with me because I'm saying this, but if we were at Tottenham and broke the rules I'd admit the same." How else were Chelsea punished for rule breaches? On top of the reduced fine, Chelsea received two transfer bans. A one-year ban was suspended for two years, while there also a nine-month suspension on signing academy players imposed. This punishment, which also carried a £750,000 fine, was in relation to the registration of academy players between 2019 and 2022. The Premier League acknowledged Chelsea's "exceptional cooperation" and "pro-active self-reporting". Pochettino is currently managing of the United States national team and took charge at the World Cup on home soil in the summer.

title_original: Martin Odegaard verbally savages Jamie Carragher and Micah Richards during live CBS Sports interview
body_original: Martin Odegaard didn't hold back during his CBS Sports interview with a comment brutally snubbing Jamie Carragher and Micah Richards. On Wednesday night, Arsenal secured a win in their Champions League opener against Napoli with a late goal from captain Odegaard securing the three points at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona. As always, the beloved CBS Sports of Kate Scott, Jamie Carragher, Thierry Henry and Micah Richards covered the match, speaking to Odegaard post-match in an interview that left Carragher and Richards at a loss for words. READ MORE: CBS Sports studio left in stitches as Jamie Carragher makes cheeky reference to bankruptcy issues Martin Odegaard brutally snubs Carragher and Richards on CBS Sports In recent years, Carragher, who Scott referred to as a Liverpool legend during the season-opening show, has been highly critical of the Arsenal captain. Perhaps most famously, Carragher brutally spoke out against Odegaard for taking a picture on the pitch after Arsenal's win over Liverpool back in the 2024/25 season. Therefore, when Richards decided to ask Odegaard who his favourite host on the show was, as is always the case on CBS Sports broadcasts, the midfielder took the chance to have a subtle dig at Carragher. The Arsenal star replied: “There’s only one answer here.” To which Carragher jokely said: “Thank you.” Odegaard then shut him down brutally, adding: “There’s only one real legend in that studio." Clearly referring to Henry, the comments left the whole studio in stitches, before Odegaard eventually admitted that he was only messing around and gave a surprising answer. “Nah, I’m joking. Jamie, you’re my favourite," Odegaard revealed. "There's only one real legend in that studio." 🤣 Martin Ødegaard brought the jokes 😂 pic.twitter.com/dglkwBcSb4 — CBS Sports Golazo ⚽️ (@CBSSportsGolazo) September 9, 2026 READ MORE: Liverpool fans say their first January transfer is done already after Atletico Madrid comeback Kylian Mbappe didn't hesitate when asked his favourite CBS Sports pundit On Tuesday night, Real Madrid also got their Champions League campaign off to a stellar start with a 2-1 win over Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu. As conversations about who could win this year's Ballon d'Or continue to heat up, Real Madrid star Mbappe ensured he was at the front of everybody's mind as he opened the scoring in the match, netting his 70th goal in the competition. Post-match, he appeared on CBS Sports for the first time to speak with the panel about the match and life under new manager Jose Mourinho. And, like Odegaard, Richards took the chance to ask the striker who his favourite pundit on the show was, with many likely assuming he would say fellow Frenchman Henry. But, after Mbappe buttering up with a special poem, Richards has given the award, with Mbappe replying: "I would have to say you." Delighted, Richards started doing laps around the studio and even hugged Mbappe through the screen in a sign of appreciation for the star player. title_original: Arsenal set to wear special lucky kit not seen since 2022 against Napoli tonight
body_original: Arsenal will wear a kit combination not seen since 2022 when they take on Napoli tonight - and it carries particular significance to manager Mikel Arteta and several players. The Gunners face Napoli at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in their first Champions League group stage match of the new season. Their chosen kit is a lucky omen for Arsenal , as they haven't lost a single match while wearing it since all the way back in 2017. READ NEXT: Arsenal's 21-player summer transfer list leaked as two Spurs players included Why Arsenal have chosen rare kit for Napoli clash Arsenal will wear an all-red strip when they take on Napoli due to UEFA 's regulations. It means that, because Napoli's home kit features white shorts, Arsenal cannot wear their usual white gear and must switch to red instead. It's not the first time Arsenal have had to change their kit to avoid a clash against the same opponents. They did so for the second leg of their Europa League quarter-final second leg fixture against Napoli in 2019. Leading 2-0 from the first leg, Alexandre Lacazette scored the only goal of the game on 36 minutes. In 2022, they also adorned an all-red strip against Watford, which they won 3-2. They drew 1-1 against West Brom while wearing the kit in 2017. Gabriel Magalhaes wearing an all-red kit during Arsenal's 3-2 win at Watford in 2022 (Image: Getty) The Gunners used the all-red kit during their UEFA Youth League clash against Napoli earlier on Wednesday, which they won 2-1. READ NEXT: Emi Martinez sparks chaotic scenes outside Emirates after Arsenal vs Chelsea as footage emerges Arsenal and Napoli have faced off twice previously in the Champions League, under the old group system during the 2013/14 season. Arsene Wenger's side won their first match 2-0 at the Emirates Stadium, with Mesut Ozil and Olivier Giroud scoring inside the opening 15 minutes. But they lost 2-0 in the return group fixture, with Gonzalo Higuain and Jose Callejon scoring late on. Napoli coach names Arsenal's 'greatest strength' ahead of Champions League clash Napoli will have a new head coach in the dugout when they take on Arsenal, with Antonio Conte having left the role at the end of last season. In what seems to be the revolving door of elite Italian managers in Serie A, he has been replaced by Massimiliano Allegri, who was formerly in charge of Juventus (twice) and was sacked by AC Milan at the end of last season after his second spell in charge. Allegri spoke highly of Arsenal and Arteta in his pre-match press conference ahead of the game, describing the Gunners' defensive qualities as their 'major strength'. READ NEXT: Mikel Arteta accused of getting away with strict Premier League rule against Chelsea "We know the difficulties of this match, which we must go into with pride and the desire to do well," he stated. "He [Arteta] did well to sort out their defence, as Arsenal concede very few goals and they work together as a team. It's their greatest strength. "We are up against one of the best. Europe gives you different motivation and adrenaline. We've got to take it one step at a time, but also have faith, because the Champions League is an ambition we must all have. This will push us forward."

title_original: Ex-Liverpool youngster once called 'magnificent' by Steven Gerrard is looking for next club on LinkedIn at 28
body_original: Former Liverpool and Arsenal midfielder Ovie Ejaria has taken to LinkedIn as he searches for a new club in his professional football career. The 28-year-old was playing for Real Oviedo in La Liga last season but became a free agent when his contract expired at the end of the campaign. Ejaria has taken the unusual step of posting on social media in an effort to attract interest in his signature. He has listed himself as a central midfielder but is also willing to play on the left wing as he looks for a new challenge. Ovie Ejaria searching for new club on LinkedIn Ejaria is a graduate of the Arsenal academy and is still based in London after his solitary year in Spain with Oviedo. He made eight appearances in La Liga last season but struggled for fitness after suffering an injury in December that left him sidelined for two months. With spells at Sunderland, Rangers and Reading also under his belt, Ejaria is a talented player who is sure to appeal to numerous clubs. Although the summer transfer window has closed, he is still free to sign for a club, provided they have space in their 25-man squad. In a post on LinkedIn, the former Liverpool player wrote: "I'm currently a free agent and looking for the right opportunity. "I'm keeping the details brief for now, but if there's an opportunity or you know of a club looking for [a] midfielder - (6, 8 & 10) or someone who can play as a left winger, please feel free to DM me. All enquiries welcome." Steven Gerrard's high praise for Ovie Ejaria Ejaria moved to Liverpool as a youth player after spending nine years with boyhood club Arsenal. He made two Premier League appearances during his time at Anfield, along with a further three in the FA Cup. Ejaria was sent out on three loan spells during his time with Liverpool, one of which was to Scottish giants Rangers. It was during his time at Ibrox that he was managed by Liverpool legend Steven Gerrard. Ejaria made 28 appearances and scored two goals before his loan spell was cut short just months into the new season. Despite the disappointing end to his time in Scotland, Ejaria still caught Gerrard's eye, with the former Liverpool captain heaping praise on the youngster following his performance against Ufa in the Europa League. "I thought he was magnificent and I think that is his strongest 90 minutes that he has given us so far," Gerrard said in August 2018. "I think we have seen a lot of flashes and a lot of halves, some good performances, but I think that's his first real excellent performance that he's announced against a good team. I thought he was excellent from start to finish." Following his release from Liverpool in 2020, the midfielder signed for Championship club Reading, where he spent the next three years. He left the club in December 2023 and remained a free agent until joining Oviedo in July 2025.

title_original: Non-league star who smashed Jamie Vardy's transfer record makes debut for new club
body_original: The highlights of the non-league star who obliterated Jamie Vardy's transfer record have impressed fans after Abdul Abdulmalik got his dream move. Vardy is easily the biggest success story of a player who came through the lower echelons of English football, playing for Stockbridge Park Steels and then Halifax Town. He then stepped up to Fleetwood Town in the Conference, now the National League, before joining Leicester City for a fee of £1million in 2012. READ NEXT: Jamie Vardy's transfer record finally broken after 14 years as eye-watering bid accepted Vardy made history by going on to make Premier League history, winning the title in incredible fashion with Leicester in 2016. He also bagged a Premier League Golden Boot and played for England at a World Cup. Record-breaking Non League star stuns fans in professional debut But the latest sensation to come out of Non-League is Abdulmalik, who had 28 goals and assists for Boreham Wood last season as they won National League Cup and were beaten in the play-off final by Rochdale at Wembley. He was the subject of strong interest from clubs in Europe in the summer, with fifth tier Boreham Wood rejecting two bids from Swedish side Djurgardens. Eventually, after the Millwall academy product issued a statement on how he was desperate for the opportunity, an offer 'in excess' of £1.5 million was accepted. The 23-year-old made his debut for his new club on Thursday, with Abdulmalik coming off the bench in a 7-1 rout over Haninge in the Swedish Cup. One compilation of his performance racked up a whopping 2.7 million viewers. The left winger was greeted by huge cheers when he entered the fray in the 61st minute and lit up the second half with a series of incredible dribbles. 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿💥 The DEBUT of 𝗔𝗕𝗗𝗨𝗟 𝗔𝗕𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗠𝗔𝗟𝗜𝗞 (𝟮𝟯) for Djurgardens after being signed from Boreham Wood. pic.twitter.com/QK3r2VZJvT — Rising Stars XI (@RisingStarXI) September 10, 2026 Abdulmalik got fans off the edge of their seat by displaying frightening pace and skill to constantly take on players. His exciting and positive cameo was enough to convince many that his career may well continue to progress if he continues in the same vein. One fan on X wrote: "He needs European football, and I guarantee he'll be in the big leagues." A second said: "Mad how no British team took a punt on him because from the clips flying around he looks class." A third added: "Such a sharp footballer. Just looks a different level, I know it’s against weaker opposition but I am so intrigued to see how he gets on." READ MORE: Jamie Vardy blocked from making Burnley debut against Wrexham due to little-known rule Abdul Abdulmalik's tough journey to make professional debut There are plenty of gems plying their trade outside of league football in England and Abdulmalik is a prime example. He represented England at Under 17 level and progressed through the age group at the Millwall academy. He was a part of the Under 21 side which won consecutive Professional Development League titles but did not make a first-team appearance for the club. Abdulmalik was released in July 2024 and went straight into Non League, where he already had experience after a loan spell with Wealdstone. He shone at Boreham Wood and was named in the National League Team of the Season last term. Having faced rejection earlier in his career, Abdulmalik is now a professional footballer and it looks like he may well be on the up.

title_original: Why Bryan Mbeumo, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro are wearing different kits to Man Utd teammates vs Sabah
body_original: The new Champions League sleeve patch was seen at Old Trafford on Thursday night as Bryan Mbeumo, Patrick Dorgu and Leny Yoro wore the one-off kit in Manchester United's clash against Sabah. Players making their first appearance in the competition will now wear special debut patches as part of a Champions League initiative between UEFA and sports merchandising giant Fanatics. The patch incorporates the word debut into the Champions League’s iconic ‘starball’ logo and will be displayed on the sleeve of the player’s shirt. READ MORE: Sabah manager Valdas Dambrauskas used 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire' winnings to fund coaching career After the player has made their debut, the patch will be removed and handed over to Topps, the Fanatics-owned trading card company, where it will be incorporated into a one-of-a-kind card. The player will then sign the card before it is placed into a collectable pack. Unused substitutes will not be eligible, meaning a player must actually take to the pitch before their patch can be turned into a card. However, those who come off the bench to make their Champions League debut will qualify. Mbuemo made his Champions League debut on Thursday night. Image credit: Getty Ayden Heaven, for example, has been named on the bench for United 's Champions League opener against Sabah, but if Michael Carrick's decides to give him minutes, the patch will become active. Of course, each card will be unique and could command eye-watering sums on the collectors’ market, where particularly rare cards have previously sold for well over £100,000 - and, in exceptional cases, millions. The initiative is also expected to be introduced in the Women’s Champions League from next season. Which Premier League players have already worn a special patch? Arsenal summer signing Illan Meslier has yet to make his Champions League bow, so he will be hoping to wear the patch in the coming weeks after missing out against Napoli on Wednesday. Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes could be seen sporting the special debut patch in Aston Villa's 3-2 win over Club Brugge on Tuesday night. Johan Manzambi. Modou Kéba Cisse and Brian Madjo are also eligible. Jeremy Jacquet and Victor Munoz also wore the patch on Wednesday during Liverpool's clash against Atletico Madrid. Iliman Ndiaye was another Champions League debutant this week, with his substitute appearance against Porto marking a special occasion for the attacking midfielder, who joined from Everton this summer. And as mentioned above, Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu sported the special patch at Old Trafford on Thursday night. Karl Darlow, Tom Heaton, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Carlos Baleba are waiting to get their chance.

title_original: Marcus Rashford receives explanation from Barcelona behind decision to snub him for Anthony Gordon
body_original: Barcelona sporting director Deco has explained why the Catalan giants decided to sign Anthony Gordon over Marcus Rashford, a decision that sparked plenty of discussion this summer. Rashford, who joined Barcelona in July last year on a season-long loan, was a regular for the La Liga winners, notching 14 goals and 14 assists across all competitions. He impressed many onlookers throughout his loan spell, including the hard-to-please Hansi Flick, but despite his form, the Spanish club decided against activating a €30 million (£25.9m) buy option. READ MORE: Barcelona make huge Anthony Gordon transfer move after 'not normal' debut in Champions League Last month, Flick voiced his appreciation towards Rashford. The German also admitted he would "miss" Rashford , who is very much part of Michael Carrick's upcoming plans at Manchester United . "In the end, Anthony Gordon comes and from the first call with him when I spoke with him, he is on fire with Barca," said Flick in pre-season. "I'm really happy that he's on our team." Deco speaks out on decision to sign Anthony Gordon over Marcus Rashford Instead of chasing a deal for Rashford, Barca decided to spend £69.3 million (€80m) on Anthony Gordon , who has made an immediate impact at the Camp Nou, registering five assists in his first four La Liga games. This week, Barcelona sporting director Deco gave an insight into the reasoning behind their decision to sign Gordon over his England teammate. "We are extremely grateful to Rashford," Deco told RAC 1 . "He contributed a lot last season, but our idea of play is much more linked to Anthony. His style fits with what the coach is looking for. We see every training session and analyse the team "We have a clear idea of what we're looking for. One of the areas we struggled last season, without Raphinha, was that the team's energy dropped. It was lost. We needed more intensity." Anthony Gordon has made a superb start to life at Barcelona. Image credit: Getty Deco added: "We analysed a lot of wingers. Signing someone from the Premier League is almost impossible, but [Flick] was clear with what he wanted and we worked on a deal from there." Marcus Rashford's gesture to Anthony Gordon after Barcelona move was made official speaks volumes Back in June, Rashford joined up with his England teammates ahead of their World Cup campaign. Here, he could be seen speaking to Gordon, who soon revealed what the Manchester United forward said. "He was just telling me how good the lads are there, the team spirit that they have, which I heard already from the people in Barca," he told talkSPORT . “So I'm really looking forward to joining up with them. He was also telling me about the city, places to live. He's a lovely guy, very caring. So he was just giving me a bit of information.” Gordon also opened up about his move to Barcelona, a team he described as the biggest in the world. “I'm not satisfied at all to just play for Barcelona," he added. "I want to win everything. This is where my career begins in my mind. So I'm at the stage I always said I was going to be."

title_original: Liverpool fans decide their first January signing is already done after Atletico Madrid comeback
body_original: Liverpool fans have declared that their first January signing is already completed after their 2-1 comeback win over Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. Marcos Llorente opened the scoring for Atletico in the first half, but Dominik Szoboszlai made it 1-1 five minutes before the half-time interval. It took the same amount of time after the break for Liverpool to take the lead, with fellow midfielder Alexis Mac Allister's thunderbolt strike from 22 yards making it 2-1. Reds supporters were particularly impressed by the performance of Ronald Araujo, who is on a season-long loan from Barcelona with an option to buy. READ MORE: Liverpool learn Ronald Araujo transfer price after loan deal confirmed 'I've seen enough...' - Liverpool told they have to sign Ronald Araujo Araujo was starting his second consecutive game for Liverpool after he played 90 minutes in Friday's 2-0 win over Ipswich Town at Portman Road. The Uruguay international assisted Szoboszlai's goal with a superb backheel, and looked imperious defensively while being calm and composed on the ball. Araujo is primarily a centre-back but is filling in at right-back - a position he is comfortable in - due to Conor Bradley and Joe Gomez's injuries and Jeremie Frimpong's poor form. Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola congratulates Ronald Araujo after the 2-1 Champions League win over Atletico Madrid (Image: Getty) Liverpool can activate an option to buy the 27-year-old for a fee of €55 million (around £47 million), and Reds fans have decided that the clause will be triggered at the first possible opportunity after an impressive performance at Anfield. "Tomorrow morning I see the transfer for Araujo," one wrote. "Ronald Araujo is going to end up being one of Liverpool's greatest ever loan deals," a second said. "I'm close to 100 per cent certain we'll trigger his €47m permanent deal clause next summer." "They lied about Araujo, this guy is phenomenal," a third stated. While a fourth wrote: "Araujo just delivered a BOSS performance. Liverpool need to trigger the clause tonight. Thanks, Barca." "I've seen enough, activate the clause," a fifth demanded. And another went one step further: "I WANT US TO LIFT THIS CLAUSE TONIGHT. WHO IS THIS PLAYER? VISCA BARCA. VISCA CATALUNYA." READ NEXT: Liverpool agree record-breaking £300m shirt deal that is 'most valuable in Premier League history' Liverpool are considering Ronald Araujo permanent deal Prior to the Champions League win over Atletico, Spanish outlet SPORT reported that Liverpool have been 'delighted' with Araujo's start to life at Anfield. He was told by Barca manager Hansi Flick that he was not part of his plans for the upcoming season, but is clearly very much in Reds head coach Andoni Iraola's plans. It has been claimed that Liverpool see Araujo as a 'necessary addition' and that there is 'a consensus among the club's hierarchy that it was the right move' to sign him on loan. "Liverpool are confident they haven't made a mistake," the report adds. "Araujo has exceeded expectations, and both the manager and the board are genuinely pleased with their signing. They expect complete success." A permanent deal is 'not out of the question', it is stated. In his first interview as a Liverpool player, Araujo told the Reds' official website that he felt his style of play would be 'perfect' for the Premier League. "I think my attributes will suit this league down to the ground," he said. "I think the style of play in the English league should be perfect for my qualities as a player. READ NEXT: The heartwarming reason Ronald Araujo has chosen the No.33 shirt at Liverpool "It's a league I've wanted to play in for a long time. It's very, very competitive and some say - and why not? - it's the best league in the world. So I'm full of excitement, I'm full of hope."

title_original: Rodri issues public apology after Barcelona vs Feyenoord over incident caught on camera
body_original: Barcelona midfielder Rodri has issued a public apology following his side's 5-1 Champions League win against Feyenoord after he was heavily criticised for an incident related to Valencia. Barca thrashed Valencia 5-0 in La Liga on Sunday, with Raphinha scoring a brace for Les Cules at Estadi de Mestalla. But after the full-time whistle, Rodri was caught on camera in conversation with Barcelona team-mate Pau Cubarsi, where he was quoted by Movistar+ as stating: "They're [Valencia] really weak. They're really weak, man. Really weak, mate." READ NEXT: Rodri's reaction to Anthony Gordon's unbelievable assist is going viral Rodri apologises to Valencia fans and players Though Valencia no longer reach the heights they did in the early and mid-2010s, particularly under Unai Emery, they did finish in the top half of La Liga last season. They even beat Barcelona 3-1 at home on the final day of the campaign. However, Carlos Corberan's side currently sit bottom of the Spanish top division, having lost three and drawn one of their opening four matches. Rodri's remarks understandably did not go down well among the club's supporters. It was reported by various Spanish outlets on Wednesday that the former Manchester City midfielder had personally called Valencia captain, Jose Gaya, to apologise for his remarks. Now, Rodri has publicly apologised in an interview following the Feyenoord win, accepting that he made a 'mistake'. READ NEXT: Anthony Gordon has everyone in agreement over what he did during Champions League debut "I want to apologise to the fans and players of Valencia," he said ( as per Fabrizio Romano ). "I also called Valencia's captain, Gaya. "A human, when they make a mistake, must apologise. I hope Valencia returns to where they belong." Rodri is on 2026 Ballon d'Or shortlist Rodri is one of three Barcelona players nominated for the men's Ballon d'Or award for 2026, with Spain compatriots Pau Cubarsi and Lamine Yamal also on the shortlist. Ferran Torres, who now plays for PSG, has also been nominated, but he spent the 2025/26 season with Barcelona and won the World Cup with Spain. Six Barcelona players have been nominated for the women's award, with Esmee Brugts, Cata Coll, Caroline Graham Hansen, Claudia Pina, Patri Guijarro and Ewa Pajor all on the shortlist. A Barca player has won either the men's or the women's awards every year since 2019, though that may change this year. Alexia Putellas is the favourite to win the women's award but moved to London City Lionesses in the summer, while Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane is currently favourite to win the men's award ahead of Yamal. Rodri won the Ballon d'Or in 2024, and was awarded the Golden Ball for the best player at this summer's World Cup to boost his chances of winning. He won both domestic cups with Manchester City as well, but his lack of game time in comparison to other top stars - he only made 30 appearances in all competitions due to injury issues - could count against him in the voting. READ NEXT: Ballon d'Or 2026 nominees announced in full as two players from surprise league make final cut

title_original: Bruno Fernandes injury concern with Man Utd star spotted limping ahead of derby
body_original: Fernandes played the full 90 minutes on Thursday (Picture: Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock) Bruno Fernandes left Old Trafford with what appeared to be a limp after Manchester United ’s Champions League victory over Sabah on Thursday night. The skipper was on the scoresheet again as United marked their return to European action with a thumping 4-0 victory over the Azerbaijan outfit. United were in control at half-time with Michael Carrick making changes in the second-half of Sunday’s derby showdown with Manchester City . Youri Tielemans was replaced at the break by Mason Mount with Andrey Santos coming on for Kobbie Mainoo just after the hour mark. Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko – two others hopeful of starting against Enzo Maresca’s side this weekend – also came off but Fernandes remained on the pitch until the final whistle. The 32-year-old was on the receiving end of some heavy challenges during the game with video footage captured outside Old Trafford appearing to show him leaving the stadium with a slight limp. The Portugal international is seen moving gingerly before waving to the crowd. Fernandes has missed just five games through injury since joining United in January 2020 with a hamstring issue ruling him out for three of those last season. Bruno Fernandes leaves Old Trafford with a limp after game vs Sabah! #brunofernandes #theeyetest #manchesterunited #bruno #fernandes pic.twitter.com/zA38v5yvuS — Theeyetest (@TheEyeTest_1) September 10, 2026 United will remain without Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba for the visit of City with the former still recovering from a knock he picked up just days before the start of the new season. Baleba meanwhile is working his way back from an ankle injury he suffered during Brighton’s pre-season campaign. Fernandes has played every minute this season (Picture:: Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock) Luke Shaw was left out of the squad on Thursday night having missed training the previous day. United later clarified his absence was due to a ‘designated rest day’ with Carrick later revealing the left-back felt some discomfort in the draw with Everton last Sunday. Shaw did not play on Thursday night (Picture: Getty) ‘He came off the other day [at Everton] with a little bit of cramp,’ Carrick said on Thursday. ‘We didn’t want to take any risks really. title_original: Enzo Maresca gives Nico O’Reilly injury update ahead of Man Utd vs Man City
body_original: Nico O’Reilly has missed Man City’s last two games with a back injury (Photo: Getty) Enzo Maresca has given an update on Nico O’Reilly’s injury ahead of Manchester City ’s huge Premier League clash against Manchester United . The latest edition of the Manchester derby takes place on Sunday at Old Trafford , with City looking to extend their lead at the top of the table. Maresca has won his first three league games in the Citizens dugout, with his side level on points and goal difference with Arsenal , and ahead by virtue of scoring one more goal. United have had a tough start to the season but City have won just two of the last six Manchester derbies and it’s been three years since they last triumphed at Old Trafford. Sign up for In The Mixer, Metro's football newsletter Get exclusive analysis and previews of the biggest games every Friday. Sign up now for free. But Maresca has been handed a timely boost, with O’Reilly passed fit to play having been sidelined for the last week with a back injury. The England international, a popular pick on Fantasy Premier League , suffered the injury during the warm-up before the 1-0 win over Coventry and then missed Tuesday’s Champions League victory at Porto. Speaking in his pre-match press conference on Friday, Maresca said the left-back/midfielder was ‘100 per cent available’ to play against United. Jeremy Doku has not played since the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal (Photo: Getty) However, the Italian also confirmed that Jeremy Doku will miss the derby, as the winger ‘needs a few more days’ before he is fully recovered from a calf injury. While this is Maresca’s first Manchester derby as City manager, it is far from his first experience of the fixture, having previously served as Pep Guardiola’s assistant. ‘It is very important for different reasons. We know how important a derby is, especially here,’ he said of the fixture. ‘A special game. The most important thing we can do is try to be ourselves and then we see the final result. ‘I have been involved in different derbies. I promise you the worst one is Olympiakos vs Panathinaikos. I promise you that is very hot! ‘It’s very important [to beat United]. It’s my first derby and I want to win the game.’ For more stories like this, check our sport page .
