title_original: Bayern Munich confirm transfer interest in Liverpool and Barcelona signings
body_original: Bayern Munich were interested in Bradley Barcola this summer (Picture: PA) Bayern Munich board member for sport Max Eberl has confirmed that the club explored a move for Liverpool new boy Bradley Barcola but were ultimately priced out of a summer deal. Mohamed Salah brought his glittering nine-year spell on Merseyside to an end last season and determined to fill the void left by the Egyptian’s departure, Liverpool’s hierarchy drew up a shortlist of potential attacking reinforcements. Barcola – a two-time Champions League winner with Paris Saint-Germain – emerged as the Reds’ primary target before too long and the player himself made it clear he was keen to push through a switch to Anfield. The likes of Arsenal and Bayern Munich were also tentatively linked with Barcola but Liverpool remained at the front of the queue as the transfer deadline came into view, before wrapping up a £123million agreement for the France international. Sign up for In The Mixer, Metro's football newsletter Get exclusive analysis and previews of the biggest games every Friday. Sign up now for free. Barcola went on to make his Liverpool debut in the side’s 2-0 victory away to Ipswich last Friday, coming off the bench for fellow summer signing Victor Munoz with half-an-hour remaining at Portman Road. And on Wednesday night, the 24-year-old started for the first time as Andoni Iraola ’s men kicked off their Champions League group-stage campaign with a 2-1 win at home to Diego Simeone’s Atletico Madrid . Barcola showed flashes of his undoubted quality in front of the Anfield faithful before being forced off with cramp ten minutes after Alexis Mac Allister’s decisive second-half strike. Liverpool signed Barcola from PSG for a fee of £123m (Picture: Getty) The Frenchman made his full debut in the Reds’ Champions League clash with Atleti (Picture: Getty) If Eberl had his way, though, Barcola would be pulling on Bayern’s colours this season, with the 52-year-old director revealing to Sport Bild : ‘To be honest, I already know Bradley from my time at Leipzig. I wanted to bring him to Leipzig. ‘We sat down together and discussed it back then. That’s how I developed a closer relationship with Bradley. ‘So there was always interest there. Of course, we also looked into him at Bayern.’ Eberl also tried to sign Barcola when he was at RB Leipzig (Picture: DeFodi Images/Shutterstock) Liverpool’s eye-watering £123m deal for Barcola saw the Frenchman become the second-most expensive player in the club’s history behind record signing Alexander Isak. ‘When you hear about sums like that, it was too much for us,’ Eberl added. ‘With Luis Diaz, we made a decision that was also costly, but on a different scale than Bradley.’ Bayern did not follow up on their initial interest in Gordon (Picture: Getty) In addition to Barcola, the Bundesliga champions also mulled over a move for Anthony Gordon before the Englishman left Newcastle to join Barcelona in a £69m deal. ‘It’s no secret that we were interested in Anthony Gordon for the left wing,’ Eberl went on. ‘We decided we were not doing that because he was simply too expensive.’ Bayern made three additions to Vincent Kompany’s first-team squad this summer, with Ismael Saibari, Nathaniel Brown and Bara Sapoko Ndiaye signing on the dotted line. Joao Palhinha, Noel Aseko, Daniel Peretz, Alexander Nubel, Jonah Kusi-Asare, Maurice Krattenmacher and Lovro Zvornarek all brought their spells at the Allianz Arena to an end. title_original: Why Liverpool missed out on the Chelsea summer signing they also wanted
body_original: Andoni Iraola could have had another option at right-back this season (Picture: Shutterstock) Chelsea summer signing Marco Palestra was also a target for Liverpool , but they could not make a move for the man the Blues paid £47 million for. Palestra moved to Stamford Bridge from Atalanta over the summer , in one of Xabi Alonso ’s first major signings as Chelsea boss. The 21-year-old does not have a great amount of experience, most of which came during last season on loan at Cagliari, where he made 37 appearances in all competitions. The right-back did enough in that season to earn his first two caps for Italy , won in March this year, and ultimately a huge move to the Premier League . Sign up for In The Mixer, Metro's football newsletter Get exclusive analysis and previews of the biggest games every Friday. Sign up now for free. Injury has caused his early Chelsea career to stall, but he did impress in pre-season and hopes to make his competitive debut for the Blues soon. Chelsea was not the only club interested in the Italian over the summer, with Liverpool also believed to have him on their shopping list before he moved to England . The Athletic report that the Reds ‘explored the possibility of challenging Chelsea’ for the signing of Palestra over the last transfer window. Marco Palestra featured and impressed in pre-season (Picture: Shutterstock) Liverpool never followed through with the interest as their priorities were elsewhere in the transfer market. After the departure of Mohamed Salah, the Reds needed to sign wide forwards, while the deal to bring in centre-back Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes was already agreed but went through over the summer. Bradley Barcola proved to be the headline signing of the window, arriving from Paris Saint-Germain for £106m , while Victor Munoz also joined from Osasuna for £34.5m. Jeremie Frimpong remains first choice at right-back, with Conor Bradley not expected back from his long-term knee injury until November. Marco Palestra has watched from the sidelines so far at Chelsea (Picture: Shutterstock) Palestra – who was also linked with a move to Inter Milan over the summer – is expected to feature regularly under Alonso this season when he has recovered from a knock picked up in training. Speaking of the Italian’s spell on the sidelines, Alonso said this week: ‘It’s especially [frustrating] for him. He came with huge energy, huge desire to enjoy his game in the Premier League. ‘He had a very good pre-season and a few days before the first game against Fulham, he picked up an injury. ‘It’s part of the life of a football player to come back from injury and we will need him for sure. He has great potential and will add a lot of good qualities we need in the team.’ Chelsea host Hull City in the Premier League and there remains a chance Palestra could feature in the squad for the first time. title_original: Ex-Chelsea and Manchester United star Juan Mata becomes free agent and instantly lands new job
body_original: Melbourne Victory have announced Juan Mata has officially ended his time at the club as a player. However, Mata’s association with Victory will continue. Mata’s one-season stint proved he has plenty of magic left in his boots Getty The club confirmed Mata will now ‘concentrate his expertise with Victory on his position in the club’s ownership group’. Mata will also take up the position as chair of Victory’s newly-established football committee. Juan Mata issues statement after leaving Melbourne Victory “I loved every minute and so greatly enjoyed everything that we achieved last season, falling back in love with football at such a special place, in an amazing city that it was a privilege to call home,” Mata said. “Thanks to my teammates, the staff and the Board for welcoming me so warmly, supporting me so generously, and allowing me to give my best for this wonderful Club and the amazing members and fans whose support I still feel every day. “Now I am excited about our next chapters, believing together in the future of Australian football and inspiring the next generation of Melbourne Victory players and supporters.” Victory’s director of football John Didulica added: “Juan’s 2025/26 season will live long in the memory of Victory fans and should be cherished by all supporters of the world’s game here in Australia. “The way he performed on the pitch and the way he conducted himself around the Club were both exemplary. “We thank him for everything he delivered and were delighted that, after he chose to join Melbourne Victory, he was able to excel within the strong culture and high-performance environment established here over several years. “Everyone at the Club is excited that he is part of our ownership group and, in the future, looks forward to his football intelligence leading our football committee.” Has Juan Mata retired? Despite Mata stepping into more administrative roles with Victory, he has not hung up his boots just yet. Mata’s 12 assists for the Victory was the most he’d contributed in a single season since the 2012/13 campaign Getty The Spanish star is now back in Europe as he considers the next steps in his career. Mata leaves the Victorian outfit after just one season, although it was one in which he reminded the world of his play-making brilliance. The 38-year-old registered five goals and 12 assists in 25 appearances for Victory in the 2025/26 campaign, earning him the Johnny Warren Medal, which is given to the A-League’s most valuable player. Mata also earned an inclusion in the PFA’s Team of the Season and was named the A-League Playmaker of the Year, further underlining his brilliance for the Victory. Sadly Mata could not add to his trophy cabinet while in Melbourne, as the Victory were knocked out in the elimination final by Sydney FC. Who else has Juan Mata played for in his career? Mata is now on the lookout for his eighth different club in a playing career that has spanned England, Turkey, Japan and Australia. Mata brings Champions League expertise to wherever he lands next Getty He began his senior career in Spain with Valencia before Chelsea came calling in 2011. Mata enjoyed two-and-a-half seasons at Stamford Bridge, only to join Manchester United . The Spaniard remained with the Red Devils until 2022, when he joined Galatasaray. Moves to Japanese side Vissel Kobe and A-League club Western Sydney Wanderers followed before he wound up with the Victory.

title_original: Darren Fletcher seen confronting abusive Man United fan immediately after Champions League win
body_original: Darren Fletcher was applauded by Man United fans for putting an abusive supporter in their place on Thursday night. The Red Devils returned to the Champions League with a 4-0 win over Azerbaijani minnows Sabah . Fletcher is a hugely popular figure at United from his playing days and his time as interim manager Getty Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes , Benjamin Sesko and Lisandro Martinez saw Michael Carrick ‘s side cruise to a comfortable victory. However, there were some unsavoury scenes after the match as players made their way home from Old Trafford. Fletcher, who is currently head coach of United’s Under-18s, was seen verbally confronting a supporter near the first-team coach. “Listen, it doesn’t matter, you can’t speak like that,” an angry Fletcher said. View Tweet: https://x.com/hashtag/mufc?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw “Show some respect. You’re the reason people don’t sign.” It appears the argument began after Man United players decided not to stop and sign autographs. While the fan continued to protest, it was not clear exactly what was said to spark the row. Other supporters in the video cheered ex-United midfielder Fletcher for backing the players and chanted his name. Manchester City next On the pitch, Carrick watched Sesko score for the second consecutive game after his return from injury. However, the United boss did not reveal whether the Slovenian striker would get his first Premier League start when the Red Devils host Manchester City in the derby on Sunday. The return of Sesko has been a huge boost for Carrick Getty Cunha has started up front in the top-flight so far this season, with Marcus Rashford and Patrick Dorgu utilised on the left side of attack. “It’s not an easy decision, of course it’s not,” Carrick said. “But it’s definitely one I’d prefer: to have goals in the team and for the boys to be playing well. “The understanding they all have is that sometimes it’s going to be a start, sometimes it’s going to be finishing the game. “We need that within the group, from game to game over the season, to be able to call upon slightly different kind of things at different times. “It’s fantastic they’re all in good form and started so well.”

title_original: Stunned Fenerbahce player has to double take during interview after learning manager resigned
body_original: Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown couldn’t believe what he heard when told his manager had instantly quit post-match. Ismail Kartal announced that he would be resigning from his post straight after a draw with Roma in the Champions League . Brown was completely baffled by the news that his manager had quit Speaking in his post-match press conference, Kartal shockingly confirmed that he would be stepping down. It caught everyone off guard – even his own players – with Brown being left completely baffled during his own interview . As he stood in front of journalist, he was told by a translator from the Fenerbahce staff that Kartal had left. And as soon as he heard, Brown quickly swung his head around with a confused expression, asking: “What do you mean he resigned?” The Birmingham-born defender then looked around as he took the news in, with it being confirmed that Kartal announced he had quit during his press conference. Brown then asked again, to make sure nothing had been lost in translation. “He quit as coach? “What do you mean by resigned… he’s not coach anymore?” Clarifying it had happened in his press conference around the same time as he was speaking, he added: “I didn’t know about this.” Kartal’s resignation marked a disappointing end to a productive night for Brown, who had scored in Fenerbahce’s draw. In fact, the left-back won the Player of the Match award following the 1-1- draw with Serie A side Roma in Istanbul. His strike just after half time helped his side claim a point in their league phase opener. View Tweet: https://t.co/Iq8hZO7pDE Kartal quit his job when speaking to the media post-match on Thursday Getty Why did Ismail Kartal resign? Fenerbahce manager Kartal left his job minutes after the full-time whistle and vowed never to return to the club. This was his fourth stint in charge of the Turkish giants. “I am resigning from my position while there is still time,” he said. “I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return. “I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players… our president and managers tried to help us in every way. Those were wonderful days. “As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning from my position. “Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today. Birmingham born Brown has never played in England but that has not stopped him competing at the highest level of club football in the Champions League Getty Brown scored as his club returned to the Champions League and he will come up against Aston Villa next Getty “I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team.” Where is Archie Brown from? The 24-year-old has never played professionally in England having come through West Brom and Derby academies. He left England at the age of 18 in 2021 to join Swiss side Lausanne-Sport. He then moved to Belgium to play for Gent where he was called up to the England U20 squad before joining Turkish side Fenerbahce in 2025 where there a number of familiar faces to Premier League fans are playing. He has cited former Arsenal and Chelsea defender Ashley Cole as the standard bearer for left-backs and even got to train with him as Cole was winding down his career at Derby. “What stood out to me the most was his approach to the game,” he told Sky Sports . “I saw his ability to laugh and joke in the changing room, but when he stepped on the training pitch or a game, it’s like a switch flicks and he’s able to get into that zone.” He has previously spoken of his desire to play in the Champions League, which he is now doing as well as competing for titles whether that is in the Premier League or on the continent.

title_original: 15-year-old wonderkid makes Manchester United history with stunning debut hat-trick
body_original: Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut on Thursday afternoon. Gabriel, who has been playing for Man United ‘s U21 side aged just 15, is arguably the hottest prospect in world football . Gabriel scored a hat-trick for Man United’s U19s against Sabah on Thursday Getty Red Devils icon Ryan Giggs labelled him a ‘generational talent’ earlier this week, and the teenager has now shown why. United’s U19s beat Sabah 5-0 ahead of the first teams’ Champions League clash , which is live on talkSPORT, with Gabriel scoring three. And by doing so, he made history for the Premier League giants. At 15 years and 339 days old, he is now the youngest ever goalscorer for the club in the UEFA Youth League, overtaking Angel Gomes, who netted in the competition aged 17 and 34 days old. Gabriel’s historic hat-trick Gabriel scored his first of the game just before half time, as he perfectly volleyed in a rebound to make it 3-0. A shot bounced back to him, forcing him to react quickly and chest the ball down, finding the back of the net with his laces. His second, which came in the 85th minute of the match, saw him take one touch in the box, neatly cut inside onto his right foot, and tuck a strike into the bottom corner. Gabriel’s third came just two minutes after, as Jim Thwaites’ lofted ball sent the young star racing through on goal. He then brushed off some pressure from the chasing defenders and broke into the box, smashing past the goalkeeper. The rising talent wheeled off to celebrate and then held three fingers aloft with the match ball after the whistle. View Tweet: https://x.com/hashtag/mufc?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw Gabriel has been labelled a generational talent and could be nearing a first-team debut Getty When could Gabriel make his first-team debut? Man United’s Gabriel continues to show why he is considered one of the best young players on the planet. So, after scoring a hat-trick on his Youth League debut, could that mean a first-team debut could be on the cards? He made his first senior appearances for the Red Devils during pre-season and has regularly trained alongside Bruno Fernandes and co. And manager Michael Carrick said in August: “JJ is one of the boys. He’s obviously got a really big talent. “He’s trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time. He’s physically adapting to each step, and we’re just continuing his development.” Should he be handed his full Man United debut before October 22, he would become the club’s youngest-ever player. Goalkeeper David Gaskell holds the record after playing his first game aged 16 years and 19 days.

title_original: West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez furiously rejects allegations he was involved in a kidnapping plot
body_original: West Ham’s Edson Alvarez has released a statement denying allegations that he was involved in a kidnapping plot. Reports in his native Mexico claimed that he was involved in the crime that was allegedly ordered by his father-in-law . Alvarez has angrily denied allegations that he was involved in a kidnapping Getty However, he has now posted on social media to furiously reject the accusation, saying it has ‘nothing to do’ with him. The 28-year-old midfielder slammed the claims and revealed that he has told his legal team to take the appropriate action. Alvarez rejects allegations in statement He wrote: “In light of the publications and statements that have circulated recently, I believe it is necessary to address this matter clearly and firmly. “I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me. “Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me. “Until now, I had chosen not to respond. “However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line. “If anyone believes they have evidence of any wrongdoing on my part, there are authorities, prosecutors, and courts before which they can present it. “Serious accusations must be supported by evidence and presented before the appropriate authorities, not through statements in media outlets whose content prioritises sensationalism and media exposure over accuracy and truth. “I will not allow my name to be used to fuel conflicts between third parties or to gain media exposure. Alvarez posted the lengthy statement on social media following the claims @edsonnalvarez Instagram “Therefore, given the seriousness of the statements that have been made, I have instructed my legal team to evaluate and pursue the appropriate legal action against any person who makes or disseminates false allegations against me. “I also want to be clear regarding the publications that have attempted to connect me to this matter through my former partner’s father: It is not my place to confirm, deny, or comment on what may be said about third parties, but it is my responsibility to make one thing absolutely clear: I have nothing to do with the events being reported. “Throughout nearly ten years of my professional career, I have made every effort to stay away from media scandals and to have my name recognised for my work both on and off the pitch. “I come from a hardworking and honourable family that taught me that a reputation is built over many years through hard work, discipline, and conduct. “For that very reason, I will not allow mine to be irresponsibly used to involve me in matters that are entirely unrelated to me. “My priority is, and will continue to be, where it has always been: my daughters, my family, and my professional career.” Alvarez has only played one game for West Ham so far this season Getty Alvarez followed up the statement with a picture of him playing for West Ham earlier this season against Portsmouth. That was his only appearance of the campaign so far for the Hammers, as he played 75 minutes in the Carabao Cup . The Mexico international, who captained his country at the World Cup in the summer, has made 74 appearances in total for the club since joining from Ajax in 2023.

title_original: Leicester warned they’re heading for ‘Armageddon’ as prospective new owner outlines plan to save them
body_original: Leicester City are heading towards financial ‘Armageddon’ without fresh capital and improved results, says prospective owner Neil Lal. The Scottish-Indian businessman, who is president of the Indian Council of the United Kingdom, is fronting a group to try and buy Leicester . Lal has issued a stark warning over Leicester’s finances amid a potential takeover Neil Lal - Linkedin Lal’s Bharat Consortium Group has three other investors, each also seeking 25 per cent of the club, with significant backing from India. “We are all wealthy businessmen,” said Lal, speaking exclusively to talkSPORT. “Rather than going through the bankers of Leicester City Football Club, we have contacted the board directly, which saves time. We have made an offer. “It is now a waiting game, but we are in contact with the club, which is a positive… our key objective is financial stability from the start.” talkSPORT understands Lal has contacted the club but has not yet spoken to Top or other senior members of the board. Leicester has set a deadline of September 14 for initial offers from interested parties, and there are at least three active groups in the process. Saudi executive Turki Alalshikh has also been sounded out following his decision in August to pull out of buying Derby County , Leicester’s east midlands rivals. Leicester owner Aiyawatt ‘Top’ Srivaddhanaprabha is seeking over £200million and, according to Lal, any new owner would also have to assume significant debt on top of that price. Leicester warned of more financial woes “In my view, the club is overvalued,” Lal, one of the leading voices promoting Scotland-India trade, explained. “Leicester is valued as a successful Championship club, and yet it’s in League One . So, for me, the valuation is over the top. “The second point is, the debt is a major concern, and the future liabilities. We have got to look at the books. That’s important. “I hope I am wrong, but I fear if something is not done quickly there could be more financial struggles ahead for Leicester.” Leicester have tasked investment banking firm CitiGroup with finding a new owner. Saudi boxing chief Alalshikh is understood to have been sounded out over a purchase Getty An eight-page pitch deck, seen by talkSPORT, emphasises Leicester’s history and facilities, and stresses the appeal of investing in the ‘third-largest English city with only one (football) club’. Leicester’s fall from grace A decade ago, the Foxes won a fairytale Premier League title under Claudio Ranieri at pre-season odds of 5000/1. Yet, they now find themselves in League One and have won only one of their opening five league games under new manager Russell Martin. The weekend’s 4-0 loss to Oxford United was a new low, and some Foxes fans have called for Martin to be sacked. “That defeat was not good,” said Lal. “It was very disappointing. It doesn’t bode well for the club. “I’d rather not say too much because, as you can appreciate, it will affect outcomes, but I understand the manager was with Rangers at one point, and he left there. “Obviously things are not going well at Leicester at the moment but we’ve got to be positive. Hopefully, things turn around. What I will say, though, is we are people of zero tolerance, and we are here for the long term.” Leicester have suffered turmoil on and off the pitch, and now play in the third tier Getty Lal sees appeal in Leicester’s storied past, but admits the Foxes must come to terms with their perilous present. He also believes Leicester’s multi-cultural community is a huge asset, and that the thriving Indian population can be better engaged with. Lal has aspirations to promote and commercialise Leicester in India where, as former Premier League winners, the club is already well known. “Leicester winning the Premier League (in 2015/16) was probably one of the greatest sporting triumphs of all time,” he said. “If someone said to me in 2014, Leicester is going to win the league, I’d have thought, ‘Okay, listen, they’ve had too much to drink. Go and see a doctor!’ “Winning the Premier League and the (2020/21) FA Cup, and doing well in Europe, was fantastic. And Leicester has a great set of loyal fans. “There is potential there. And yet there’s many things we’ve got to do to make things better. We’ve got to be profitable. We’ve got to have financial stability. We’ve got to think about winning. That’s the key thing. “We have also got to respect the tradition of what’s happened, and the late owner (Khun Vichai) , Top and the whole (Srivaddhanaprabha) family. “This is not a quick fix by just throwing the kitchen sink at it. This is a long-term strategy. It’s a five-year plan to get Leicester back to the Championship and then the Premier League, and we don’t just want to go up a division only to come back down again after a year.” Lal’s comments echo a recent statement by the Foxes Trust which called on Leicester City to “reassure supporters on the financial health and viability of the club until a sale has taken place”. Leicester were crowned as Premier League champions just a decade ago AFP or licensors Lal’s consortium are open to putting a fan representative on the board and also plan to consult several Leicester legends on key club decisions. “I’ll definitely consider that (putting a fan on the board),” said Lal. “I understand where the Foxes Trust are coming from and I agree with many of their points. “There has got to be community and fan engagement. We have got to listen to the fans. This is vital. Without the fans, we are nothing. And I think having a committee of maybe six to eight ex-Leicester footballers to discuss the buying and selling of players would be a good thing. “I’m a numbers person. I just want the club to be financially viable and profitable. But regarding recruiting players or picking managers, I think we should leave that to the experts to come back to us with suggestions. That’ll be the best way.” Several investors contacted by talkSPORT believe a sale is not just desired by Top but required. There is a danger without one Leicester are heading towards administration, which comes with an automatic 12-point deduction. The challenge for Lal, and other interested parties contacted by talkSPORT, is Leicester are yet to share the full financial picture of the club making future liabilities hard to predict before undertaking the rigorous due diligence process. This may be down to CitiGroup wishing to whittle down a shortlist of viable owners first, which is a normal step, or even a hope of jumping straight to a preferred bidder, who would then traditionally be handed an exclusive period to comb through the books. talkSPORT has learned at least two groups have walked away from the process due to concerns over the club’s debt from the limited financial information already provided. Lal’s own fear is that results on the field decline further before he has a chance to influence the club. Martin is already under pressure as the new Leicester boss amid poor results Getty “If we’re going to progress further, and Leicester is falling down (the table), it doesn’t bode well,” said Lal, who has no plans to sell off the club’s Seagrave training centre or the 32,259-capacity King Power Stadium. “If, God forbid, Leicester ever drops down to League Two, financially, it’s Armageddon. It really is. “Right now, we have a club that has a huge wage bill and debts, and it’s in League One. That’s a concern. “My fear is if this continues for the long term, over the next two-four months, and Leicester’s not playing well in the league, then unfortunately, we are going to have to review the situation and possibly walk. And I don’t want to do that… “The foundations are there, but the problem is the financial stability is not. In my humble opinion, I think the club has been a bit mismanaged.” Leicester is not the only club Lal is looking at. He is also open to investing in Rangers. Although the Foxes are his primary focus, building a multi-club network is not discounted. “Rangers are going through a bit of a tough patch at the moment,” said Lal. “New owners [Andrew Cavenagh and 49rs Enterprises] have taken over and, obviously, they need time, but there’s also financial losses. So at the end of the day, if the opportunity arises and we can come to the right price, we may look at the situation. “Unfortunately, in Scotland, the [country’s] coefficient ranking has dropped, which impacts European qualification, adding extra playoff rounds. “Rangers have huge support. It’s a wonderful club. If the opportunity arises, we may look at it. It’s Leicester right now, and then if Rangers ever comes up, let’s see what happens.” Leicester could have new ownership by the end of 2026 Getty Lal will not be afraid to make difficult decisions if successful in buying Leicester, but he is also keen to protect the legacy of both King Power and the Srivaddhanaprabha family. Part of the reason he has made a direct offer to the club, bypassing CitiGroup, is a belief that dealing directly with Top stands the best possible chance of agreeing a deal, and persuading the Leicester owner to lower his asking price. “I have total respect for Top and his late father,” said Lal. “They have put a lot of money into the club. Unfortunately, financially, the club’s not doing great right now. But we’ve got to respect that remarkable 5,000/1 win… I can assure you no one wants to erode and disrespect that legacy. “Top and his family, for me, are Leicester royalty, and they should always be part of the club… But we’ve got to be truthful as well. Integrity, character, morals, and principles are the four key points I’ll always adhere to. “Without financial stability, we can’t move forward. The problem is, and this is not only with Leicester but across many football clubs, you can’t just lose money year after year. This is why you have many clubs going to Administration, and some have actually closed completely. We can’t have that with Leicester.” It’s a worrying time for Foxes fans, both on and off the field, but sources have told talkSPORT the intent is to have a new owner in place before the season ends, and potentially even by the end of this year. Leicester were approached for comment.

title_original: Premier League star boycotts Switzerland over furious World Cup row with manager
body_original: Leeds forward Noah Okafor has revealed he will not play again for Switzerland as long as boss Murat Yakin is in charge . The 26-year-old has released a lengthy statement on social media, where he has commented on broken promises and betrayed trust. Okafor has declared he will never play under Yakin again for Switzerland’s national team Getty Okafor, who has scored twice in 26 games for the Red Crosses since making his international debut in 2019, was part of their World Cup squad in North America. What has Noah Okafor’s role been at major tournaments? Having been frozen out of selection since November 2024, the former AC Milan man was hopeful of playing a key part in North America following a season in which he scored eight Premier League goals for Leeds . But for the second major tournament in a row, he played a peripheral role – much to his dismay. The former Red Bull Salzburg star, who made three outings from the bench at the 2022 World Cup under Yakin’s tutelage, was an unused substitute in each of Switzerland’s five fixtures at Euro 2024. And in the most recent edition of football’s global tournament, Okafor was again overlooked by Yakin – making just one appearance from the bench – while remaining on the bench on five occasions. Okafor is no stranger to public fall-outs with Yakin, with the latter previously questioning his attitude and his impact on the pitch. He has now issued a statement on Instagram where he has vowed to never represent his country again – though he did hail Yakin for guiding Switzerland to the quarter-finals of the World Cup for the first time since 1954. What has Noah Okafor said about his Switzerland future? Okafor said: “Dear fans, these lines are the hardest I have written in my career so far, after careful consideration, I have decided to step back from the Swiss national team until further notice. “This decision is extremely difficult for me, but I want and must express it now, there was never anything greater for me than playing for Switzerland. “Every time I wore this jersey, I tried to leave my heart on the pitch. I would have loved to continue playing for Switzerland in the future and giving everything for our country. Okafor has been an unused substitute in ten of Switzerland’s last 11 matches in major tournaments Getty Yakin has previously questioned Okafor’s attitude Getty “But under the current circumstances, I simply can no longer do so. It is important to me to clarify one thing, this decision has nothing to do with playing minutes. “I know that I haven’t always done everything right in the past. Young players make mistakes, and I have apologized for that. But now the situation is different. “Even during the World Cup, I always accepted difficult phases and put myself at the service of the team. It was a great honour for me to be at the World Cup for my country. “I believed for a long time that the situation would change. A year after the European Championship, Murat Yakin came together with members of the coaching staff specifically to see me in England to have a clarifying conversation. “It was a very appreciative and good conversation. We were able to look forward and clear up misunderstandings. I was grateful to Murat Yakin for that. “That is precisely why I traveled to the World Cup with a good feeling, full of motivation and with the firm intention of giving everything for the team and for Switzerland. View this post on Instagram “Which made what I experienced there all the more disappointing. Not because I played very little, but because of the way I was treated. For me, it was the most difficult time of my career so far. “First off, I know that some people will now think again, ‘Ah, Okafor again, he’s just offended because he hardly played.’ “But again, my decision has nothing to do with my playing minutes. I travelled to the tournament to support my team in the best possible way – on the pitch and off it. “Things happened that deeply affected me. Trust has been broken. Promises were not kept. And when I was allowed to play against Algeria, even minor mistakes were reacted to far away from our goal in a way that deeply hurt me. “In the weeks since, I have thought a lot and decided for myself that under the current manager, I no longer want to play for the national team. “Murat Yakin is doing a great job and has achieved something historic with Switzerland. Success proves him and his work right. Okafor’s only outing in the 2026 World Cup came against Algeria – a 19-minute cameo off the bench Getty “And of course, I don’t want any special treatment from him. Only mutual respect and trust – but I don’t see this foundation for the coming years. I sincerely wish the team all the best. I am happy about every success of the team and think that we achieved great things at the World Cup. “Many of my teammates are friends, and I will continue to cheer for them and support them. “I am grateful to Switzerland for everything I was able to experience. Playing for this country was and remains something very special. “Believe me, whenever I stood on the pitch, I left my heart for this jersey. See you soon, Noah.” Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka was quick to message a love heart emoji, along with striker Breel Embolo. Okafor, who has registered one assist from five outings for Leeds this term, will be looking to open his account for the season against Newcastle next Monday night.

title_original: The biggest British football rivalries, including the only elite level city derby
body_original: Every football fan will argue that their club’s biggest and fiercest rivalry deserves its place on the UK’s ‘Mount Rushmore’ of derbies. Well, even talkSPORT has struggled to narrow the picks down to just four selections. Sports fans use Mount Rushmore – the iconic carved sculpture depicting influential US presidents – as a benchmark to list the most influential things in a specific subject – but talkSPORT argues four is not enough! Getty Every Thursday, Max will pick his definitive list using the Mount Rushmore ranking method – four iconic people, matches etc – in a variety of categories. However, four is quite hard, so he’s arguing for a fifth, which is why Max has called his Mount Rushmore-or-less . And there’s no better place to start than derbies; it’s the one every fan first looks for and is essentially a cup final within itself. Celtic vs Rangers: ‘More than just football’ Scott explained: “This is a 50-50 divide within the city, separated by the River Clyde, and it’s more than just football. “I know that’s cliché, but this is political, this is religious, and it’s the fiercest derby out there. “And that 12.30 kickoff on a Saturday or a Sunday, which is in place, by the way, for policing and safety purposes, is compulsory viewing.” Celtic and Rangers fans have been banned from attending Old Firm away matches as a result of the on-pitch clashes between supporters . “I’d much rather watch League One than Scottish football,” Scott added. “However, when it’s the Old Firm Derby, you have to watch it. And even if you’re one of these people that sits there and thinks, ‘ Rangers and Celtic wouldn’t make it out of the Championship’, you cannot deny that this, as a derby, in and of itself, is unlike anything we’ll ever see in England. Dating back to 1888, Glasgow hosts one of the fiercest derbies in football and you can guarantee there will be fireworks Getty Images - Getty As well as fiery battles on the pitch, both sets of supporters have been involved in large-scale disorder leading to away fans being banned from games PA ‘The biggest and best rivalry’ “This is partly down to the violence which we’ve seen prevent away fans from going into the stadiums. “In many ways, it’s a stain on the game, but you cannot take away from how passionate this is. “For me, watching the Old Firm Derby, it’s like a break away from a much more sanitised version of football that we get in the Premier League . “And I love the Premier League. It’s still the best league in the world, but the authentic, raw passion that you get in Glasgow on an Old Firm Derby day is unrivalled. “Arguably, it’s the fiercest, the biggest, the best rivalry in UK football in derbies!” Aston Villa vs Birmingham is ‘an absolute corker’ Scott continued: “I think people have a little bit of a recency bias because Birmingham haven’t been in the Premier League since 2011, but that doesn’t take away from how much these two clubs hate each other. What is Mount Rushmore? The faces of George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Abraham Lincoln are carved into the stone in South Dakota, chosen for their representation of the most important events in the United States’ history. As a result, fans use the idea to create their own version to list the most influential or iconic games and people that define their selected categories. Although the sides have been in different divisions, the passion between Birmingham and Villa fans remains high Getty The UK is home to some of the most fiery rivalries in world football where you can guarantee things will get heated among fans, players and coaches “St. Andrews and Villa Park are just 2.4 miles apart. It’s, in fact, the closest derby in England.” The Second City Derby hasn’t taken place since 2019, when Jack Grealish was assaulted by a Blues fan on the pitch before he scored the winner in a 1-0 triumph for Villa in the Championship. Scott said: “That catapults his career, or one of the many things to catapult his career to become a treble winner that we saw at Manchester City . “Just because it’s outside London, just because these two clubs aren’t always in the Premier League, doesn’t mean this isn’t an absolute corker of a rivalry.” Arsenal vs Tottenham is the only legitimate elite-level derby in London This season, there are six Premier League clubs based in the capital, which means there are 30 combinations of a London derby each year. And that’s just in the top-flight; Charlton Athletic, Millwall, Queens Park Rangers, and West Ham make up the London sides in the Championship – with all 10 sides also potentially facing each other across each of the two domestic cup competitions as well. However, Nottingham Forest fan Scott argued: “I’ve got a bee in my bonnet about Londoners trying to create a rivalry out of everything. “QPR against West Ham, it’s not a derby. The only legitimate elite-level derby in London is the North London Derby. “It’s a genuine turf war. You go back to 1913, and the Woolwich Arsenal , now Arsenal, were a South London club until they moved to Highbury, and it became a turf war. “And that’s essentially the feel I get from Arsenal and Spurs fans about how much they hate each other. It’s like a gang turf war. “This is a legitimate, fierce, massive UK rivalry. “And the irony is, this now-famous song about North London forever that Arsenal sing, it’s not legitimate. “Spurs have been the forever North London club. And so, apologies, Arsenal fans, it’s a massive derby, but Spurs were there first.” Arsenal’s move from south to north London in 1913 sparked the rivalry that has seen countless flashpoints – and Arsenal winning the league at Tottenham’s home twice Getty Statistically, the dirtiest derby in UK football It’s not the Old Firm Derby. It’s the Tyne-Wear Derby, averaging over five yellows a game and a red card every other game. “It goes all the way back to King Charles I, who essentially gave Newcastle a monopoly over the coal industry, which had an economic impact on Sunderland . That’s where this hatred begins. “And it’s not just back to the times of King Charles and Cromwell. This is industry rivalry, whether it’s coal, whether it’s shipmaking. “They’ve always been at loggerheads. They’ve always been in competition, and you see that on the football pitch. “I think they’ll probably look down on these sort of so-called London rivalries when QPR or Fulham are playing Chelsea . “It’s not a scratch on the Tyne-Wear Derby, let me tell you.” Police officers hold back a crowd of Newcastle fans outside St James’ Park prior to Sunderland’s arrival in March Getty Man United have many enemies in the Premier League, but the rivalry with Liverpool trumps that with City as well as the Merseyside derby Liverpool contest with Everton Getty What has been snubbed? “I haven’t included Millwall vs West Ham,” Scott began while leading up to his fifth and final selection. “I haven’t included the Steel City derby in Sheffield. I haven’t included the East Midlands derby, the Brian Clough derby between Forest and Derby. Haven’t included the Merseyside derby, for crying out loud…” But to add insult to Everton ‘s injury, Liverpool have been included – but against arch-rivals Manchester United . “The reason being, these are the biggest clubs in England, two of the biggest institutions in world football. “Both have got 20 titles. Liverpool, of course, have a slightly richer European history, but you think about [former managers] Fergie, Paisley, Shankly, Klopp. “They have permeated English football imagination since the get-go. Two clubs, both with their own sort of tragedies. “These are the biggest clubs in England. Nobody can argue otherwise, and therefore I can’t not have them in my Mount Rushmore – or less of UK football derbies. “It’s elite. Simple as.”

title_original: Alessandro Del Piero names Arsenal star who ‘thrived’ against Napoli
body_original: Del Piero impressed with what he saw from Arsenal (Picture: Cinquetti/NurPhoto/Shutterstock) Italy legend Alessandro Del Piero believes Arsenal were a class above Napoli in their Champions League victory over the Serie A giants. The Gunners came up just short in their bid to conquer Europe last season, beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in the final in Budapest. They got their new European campaign off to a winning start on Wednesday with a 1-0 win at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona in Naples with Martin Odegaard ’s second-half effort the difference between the two sides. The Norway international has enjoyed a superb start to the season after struggling with form and fitness at stages during last term’s title-winning campaign. Sign up for In The Mixer, Metro's football newsletter Get exclusive analysis and previews of the biggest games every Friday. Sign up now for free. Del Piero, on punditry duty for Sky Sports Italia for last night’s game; lauded Arsenal’s physical qualities and the strength of their squad with Mikel Arteta able to call upon Noni Madueke , Kai Havertz, Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis as second-half substitutes. He believes Arsenal’s approach allowed Odegaard in particular to cause havoc. ‘Napoli were the ones who were tired in the 80th minute, not Arsenal, because Arsenal kept the ball more, given their style of play,’ del Piero told Sky Sports Italia. Odegaard scored the winning goal in Naples (Picture: Cippitelli/NurPhoto/Shutterstock) ‘Players like Odegaard thrive in a game like that, having had an amazing year behind them. From a psychological standpoint, something comes into play there. ‘Saka or the Arsenal wingers could attack with fresh legs, while Napoli’s had to chase for three minutes and then be asked to turn the play around. ‘It’s not just tiredness, but the style of play, positioning, confidence, and the quality of more established players on the one hand.’ Arsenal picked up a big win on the road (Picture: Getty Images) Arsenal take on Sunderland away from home on Saturday night and return to Champions League action on 13 October when they host Lille. The Gunners head to Bayern Munich for their toughest test of the league phase in October with Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid to come at home before the year is out. title_original: Max Allegri pinpoints what Arsenal ‘are very good at’ after making Champions League claim
body_original: Allegri said Napoli were simply second best (Picture: Shutterstock) Napoli head coach Massimiliano Allergi has conceded ‘there was nothing his side could do’ up against ‘one of the strongest teams in Europe’ in Arsenal . The Gunners got their Champions League campaign off a winning start with Martin Odegaard ’s second-half goal sealing victory at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Wednesday night. Mikel Arteta ’s side were in control throughout the contest but passed up a number of opportunities to take the lead – registering 26 shots in total – before their captain stepped up. It was another defeat for Napoli who have lost three in a row in all competitions, beaten by Como and Inter in Serie A leading into last night’s game. Sign up for In The Mixer, Metro's football newsletter Get exclusive analysis and previews of the biggest games every Friday. Sign up now for free. Speaking after the game Allegri praised the strength of Arteta’s ‘extraordinary’ side, seeing little wrong in his side’s performance where they simply came up second best. The Italian also highlighted the opposition’s slick one-twos that caused problems for his side all night. ‘We played a good match against one of the strongest teams in Europe. The first half was very even, then they upped the tempo in the second,’ Allegri said. ‘We defended well; if we had defended like that against Como and Inter, we probably wouldn’t have lost. We need to look at the positives. Then, if you mess up the final pass, you risk conceding a goal, as happened. ‘I think this evening we had a good performance against an extraordinary opponent.’ Odegaard scored the game’s only goal (Picture: Shutterstock Editorial) He continued: ‘We knew it would be a tough one. We’re coming off three consecutive defeats, but we can’t get discouraged because I can’t fault the lads for anything today. When we defend like that, it’s difficult to score.’ Asked if there was anything else his side could have done, he added: ‘No, not tonight. Unfortunately, we fell for a one-two that we didn’t follow through on. They’re very good at that.’ Italy legend Alessandro del Piero meanwhile believed the physical levels of the two teams was a huge factor on the night. Arteta’s side dominated the game in Italy (Picture: Getty) ‘Napoli were the ones who were tired in the 80th minute, not Arsenal, because Arsenal kept the ball more, given their style of play,’ Del Piero told Sky Sports Italia. ‘Players like Odegaard thrive in a game like that, having had an amazing year behind them. From a psychological standpoint, something comes into play there. Saka or the Arsenal wingers could attack with fresh legs, while Napoli’s had to chase for three minutes and then be asked to turn the play around. It’s not just tiredness, but the style of play, positioning, confidence, and the quality of more established players on the one hand.’ Comment now Comments Add Metro as a Preferred Source on Google Add as preferred source

title_original: Hull player in rollover crash as car pictured upside down near training ground
body_original: Hull player Sorba Thomas has been involved in a rollover car crash outside the club’s training ground. The Wales winger’s vehicle was pictured upside down on a residential road on Friday morning. The 27-year-old was a late arrival from Stoke on September 1 Getty Sorba, who signed for the Premier League club in a £10million deal on Deadline Day, is not seriously injured. Emergency services arrived on the scene after the crash which took place close to the Tigers’ training ground in Cottingham. Fans were concerned as images of the player’s Land Rover Defender spread on social media. Details of the crash remain unclear but the vehicle had flipped onto its roof on a narrow street. Thomas’ car was pictured upside down in a residential area in worrying scenes Hull quickly released a statement to confirm Thomas escaped ‘completely unscathed’. “We are relieved to confirm that Sorba Thomas is unharmed following a road traffic accident near to the club’s Cottingham training ground,” a Hull statement read. “The club is aware of images of Sorba’s car circulating on social media and can reassure supporters that he has sustained no injuries and emerged from his vehicle completely unscathed.” Thomas only recently made his debut for Hull, coming off the bench as a late substitute in the 0-0 draw with Aston Villa last Saturday. He started the 1-0 defeat to Sunderland in the EFL Cup on Tuesday and played the full 90 minutes. While Hull have confirmed Thomas escaped unscathed physically, boss Sergej Jakirovic must decide whether he will travel with the squad to Stamford Bridge to take on Chelsea on Saturday. Thomas has featured three times for Hull since joining from Stoke Getty The newly-promoted Tigers are unbeaten and still yet to concede, but will have their work cut out against the free-scoring Blues. Sorba Thomas’ career Thomas’ summer move to Hull now sees him playing in the Premier League for the first time in his career. After starting out in West Ham’s academy, the Wales international was released aged 16 and then joined non league side Boreham Wood. He impressed over the next four years in the National League, before Huddersfield gave him a chance in the EFL in 2021. Following loan stints at Blackburn and French side Nantes, he moved to Stoke in 2025 and shone in the Championship last term. Thomas scored ten goals and assisted 13 others across 45 appearances in all competitions. Thomas starred in the EFL last term, earning him a move to Hull Getty This saw him named Stoke’s Player of the Year, as well as earning him a place in the Championship Team of the Year. His exploits in the second tier drew Premier League interest this summer, which saw Thomas’ start to the season with the Potters disrupted as Hull chased his signature. With reports of Hull agreeing a fee to sign him, sources close to him were forced to deny reports of him refusing to play for Stoke , who featured in all of the club’s first three Championship games. Ultimately, a move materialised anyway, as Thomas moved to the MKM Stadium as one of six deadline day signings.

title_original: Why there is no 12:30pm Premier League kick-off this Saturday with Arsenal clash moved
body_original: For the first time this season, there will be no early kick-off in the Premier League on Saturday afternoon. Fans have been treated to three brilliant 12:30pm matches so far this term, but they’re going to have to wait for their football this weekend. Arsenal’s clash with Sunderland was moved, meaning there is no early kick-off Getty In the opening Saturday of the campaign, Hull City shocked Manchester United , with the newly-promoted side winning 2-0 . And goals galore followed, with Liverpool and Nottingham Forest drawing 2-2 before Newcastle and Bournemouth did the same last weekend. However, there is no early game to look forward to this weekend, meaning fans have to patiently wait for the action… Why is there no early kick-off this Saturday? The Premier League have shuffled the schedule on Saturday due to the European football being played in midweek. Sunderland vs Arsenal is taking place at 8pm, exclusively live on talkSPORT, after the match was confirmed to be rescheduled in July . The match at the Stadium of Light was moved two months ago as the league pre-empted that the Gunners would be playing in the Champions League in the days prior. Mikel Arteta ‘s side beat Napoli 1-0 in Italy on Wednesday evening. Sunderland vs Arsenal was also selected for TV coverage on TNT Sports, with the broadcaster only able to use the 12:30pm and 8pm slots. Typically, if a game can’t be played early on a Saturday due to a team playing in Europe on a Wednesday or Thursday, they will instead broadcast the fixture in their late slot. In this case, Sunderland vs Arsenal was switched to the 8pm slot, which has left the early kick-off empty this weekend. Premier League schedule this weekend Saturday, September 12 Liverpool vs Fulham – 3pm Crystal Palace vs Ipswich – 3pm Bournemouth vs Brentford – 3pm Aston Villa vs Nottingham Forest – 3pm Chelsea vs Hull – 3pm Tottenham vs Everton – 5:30pm Sunderland vs Arsenal – 8pm – live on talkSPORT Sunday, September 13 Coventry vs Brighton – 1pm Manchester United vs Manchester City – 4:30pm Monday, September 14 Leeds vs Newcastle – 8pm – live on talkSPORT Arsenal’s busy schedule Arsenal will appreciate some extra recovery time following their clash with Napoli as they begin a chaotic few days. The Gunners are set to play three games in six days, starting with the Champions League match on Wednesday night. After that, they take on Sunderland on Saturday, before then coming up against Ipswich in the Carabao Cup third round. That cup fixture will take place on Tuesday, September 15, with commentary from the Emirates live on talkSPORT. Meanwhile, Sunderland are also having to play three games in seven days, as the schedule starts to get busy in England. But their toughest clash comes this weekend… Arteta’s side have three games in six days, with the Sunderland clash at 8pm on Saturday Getty Sunderland vs Arsenal on talkSPORT talkSPORT will have exclusive live coverage of Sunderland vs Arsenal at the Stadium of Light, presented by Reshmin Chowdhury. Commentary will be coming from Sam Matterface and former England striker Dean Ashton.
