title_original: England U21’s new Arjen Robben warned against Chelsea transfer from sister club
body_original: Those of a Chelsea persuasion will have fond memories of Arjen Robben – the skilful, electric, tantalising former Dutch winger. A master at beating defenders and causing danger with his left foot after drifting in from the right, Robben was a problem for defences – and England could have their own version in Sam Amo-Ameyaw. Robben is renowned as one of the best wingers in football history, and English football appear to have a like-for-like player on the rise Getty Strasbourg have turned into a hotspot for young talent and share the same owners, BlueCo, as Premier League giants Chelsea , with the club now working towards a return to the top of French football. The Ligue 1 side operate in the transfer market with a model that prioritises the signings of promising players in their teens or early 20s over established or more experienced names. Chelsea mostly worked in the same way up until the recent summer window, but Strasbourg haven’t strayed – the average age of their 18 recent arrivals is 20.4. Hermann Malonga, who was eyed by Manchester City , is one of those to have made the switch as he joined from Paris Saint-Germain, with Jacobo Ortega arriving after his spell at Real Madrid. However, with the 2026/27 season now in full flow, Strasbourg have made a strong start thanks to Amo-Ameyaw, who was one of their ‘class of summer 2025’ signings. A former academy talent at Tottenham Hotspur , he completed his move to Strasbourg from Southampton initially on loan before the obligation to buy, worth a reported €7million (£6m), was activated. On Sunday, the England U21 winger came off the bench to score two goals in a 6-2 Ligue 1 win at Troyes – both saw him burst in from the right and fire past the goalkeeper, just like Robben did in his prime. Strasbourg to Chelsea the wrong thing Continued success at Strasbourg would spark the potential for a big-money move to their affiliates Chelsea like Mamadou Sarr and Emmanuel Emegha have done of late, as well as Valentin Barco , who scored in the thrilling 6-3 win over Leeds United on Wednesday night. Chelsea and Strasbourg transfers under BlueCo 2023/24: Angelo – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Andrey Santos – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg 2024/25: Diego Moreira – transfer, Chelsea to Strasbourg Djordje Petrovic – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Caleb Wiley – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg 2025/26: Mathis Amougou – transfer, Chelsea to Strasbourg Aaron Anselmino – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Ben Chilwell – transfer, Chelsea to Strasbourg David Datro Fofana – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Kendry Paez – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Mike Penders – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Ishe Samuels-Smith – transfer, Chelsea to Strasbourg* Mamadou Sarr – transfer, Strasbourg to Chelsea (loaned back to Strasbourg until February 2026) 2026/27: Genesis Antwi – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Valentin Barco – transfer, Strasbourg to Chelsea Emmanuel Emegha – transfer, Strasbourg to Chelsea Dario Essugo – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Filip Jorgensen – loan, Chelsea to Strasbourg Omari Kellyman – transfer, Chelsea to Strasbourg Deivid Washington – transfer, Chelsea to Strasbourg *Samuels-Smith joined Strasbourg in July 2025, but transfer was reversed in September 2025 Amo-Ameyaw is on his way to holding down a key role for Strasbourg, and this could tee up a future move to Chelsea AFP High praise has seen him be touted as the new Robben, who got amongst the goals for Chelsea, Madrid, Bayern and the Netherlands by cutting onto his left with ease Getty But when European football journalist Andy Brassell reflected on his display against Troyes, he argued that, despite the glitz and glamour of the Premier League, Amo-Ameyaw should stay put. Brassell compared the 20-year-old to the Chelsea hero and Dutch legend Robben, who also starred for European giants such as Real Madrid and Bayern Munich. Robben scored 246 goals and recorded 200 assists for FC Groningen, PSV Eindhoven, Chelsea, Madrid, Bayern and the Netherlands with his unique and effective skill set – the fact that Amo-Ameyaw has been likened to him is nothing but encouraging. “Sam Amo-Ameyaw coming on and finishing the game, really, against Troyes, the ‘multi-club derby’ between Troyes and Strasbourg,” he told talkSPORT.com. “Strasbourg had a bit of a rough start in the first half; they went a goal down and were under pressure for a little bit, but they recovered from it really well. “When they came back into the game, Amo-Ameyaw was great when he came on. He went from them having an advantage in the game to then completely killing it. “He contributed nicely on many occasions last season, but you know when you can see a player has really taken a step up? He came on in this game, scored two goals on his left foot coming in from the right-hand side that Arjen Robben would have been proud of. “Two brilliant goals, the talent is absolutely clear. It’s just, with Strasbourg, you don’t know if it’s going to be kept in the place where it should develop for long enough. Amo-Ameyaw made 12 appearances for Southampton, and two of those were in the Premier League Getty “If there was some sort of Chelsea swoop for him in five months, or four months, or 12 months, it wouldn’t surprise me, but it would probably be the wrong thing at this point in time. “He’s a really interesting player, I wouldn’t want him to become just another commodity, I really enjoy watching him.” Brassell then assessed Amo-Ameyaw’s chances of playing at senior level for England if he sustains an upward trajectory at Strasbourg. He has already earned 46 total appearances across Three Lions youth sides, two of which have come at the second-highest level with the U21s. “I guess if we’re looking at it from an eventual England perspective, it is quite hard to see where you go,” Brassell explained. “We’ve got Bukayo Saka, Cole Palmer, we’ve talked about Nwaneri who, if he has a good season at (Borussia Dortmund, on loan from Arsenal ), might be in the mix too. “So, Amo-Ameyaw just needs to concentrate on having a really, really good season at club level and then take it from there. “But, given that they lost Gary O’Neil as their coach and they lost some big players, it is an opportunity for him and for them. I think they’ve looked really quite decent over these last couple of weeks.” Amo-Ameyaw, who is of Ghanaian descent, made his England youth debut in 2021 and has since scored four times Getty

title_original: ‘You need him’ – Arsenal told to ignore star’s nightmare statistic against Napoli
body_original: Arsenal fans have been urged to stick by Viktor Gyokeres despite a damning statistic from his performance against Napoli. The centre-forward endured a difficult night on Wednesday as he made his first start of the season. Gyokeres has been defended after a difficult night against Napoli in the Champions League Getty Gyokeres had previously made just two substitute appearances across all competitions this term. However, following his 12-minute cameo against Chelsea on Sunday, he was thrown in from the start in the Champions League. Arsenal went on to claim a 1-0 victory in Italy, with Martin Odegaard scoring the only goal of the game. Gyokeres played 73 minutes before being replaced by Kai Havertz , having had just nine touches. Meanwhile, of Arsenal’s 26 shots in the match, none of them were by the Sweden striker. Gyokeres defended European football journalist Kevin Hatchard has defended Gyokeres, though, on the latest episode of the talkSPORT Daily podcast. Discussing his performance with Angelina Kelly, Hatchard admitted: “I feel for him because I thought it was odd that they signed him in the first place. “Not him specifically, but a number nine, because for exactly the reasons I’ve talked about with Havertz, because it’s not generally how Arsenal play. “He wants the ball nice and early when it’s in a counter-attack. He wants to be able to have open field that he can run at people, get the ball out of his feet and shoot. It’s not how Arsenal play. “They’re quite deliberate and they play one twos around the box. They do play some expansive stuff sometimes, but they’re all about control and they’re all about when they lose the ball, being in the right place, having that really good rest defence. Gyokeres had nine touches and no shots for the Gunners on Wednesday night AFP “So by nature, they don’t like to open the game up that much and so I thought he did pretty well last season. He got 21 goals in all competitions.” Gyokeres joined Arsenal from Sporting Lisbon for £63.7million last summer, signing a five-year deal. Prior to the move, he had scored 97 goals in 102 matches during his time in Portugal. The 28-year-old has since found the net 21 times for the Gunners in 58 appearances across all competitions. Arsenal ‘need’ Gyokeres Gyokeres is yet to score in three outings this term, though, but was the club’s leading scorer in his debut season. Hatchard added: “He gets loads of stick. Look, is he a world class striker? No, no, he isn’t, but he got 20 goals for the Premier League champions, and he played a full role in them winning the Premier League because Havertz wasn’t fit very often. Gyokeres was handed his first start of the season against Napoli by Arteta Getty “So you need a guy like that who’s going to back up. Look, if they’d signed Julian (Alvarez), you wouldn’t have seen him for dust. That’s the brutality.” Arsenal held talks with Atletico Madrid last month over a potential move for forward Julian Alvarez. The Argentina international was valued at £120million this summer amid interest from Barcelona . Whilst Arsenal were prepared to launch a move of their own, Alvarez informed the Gunners he did not want to join the club . As a result, Gyokeres remained at the Emirates Stadium to compete with Havertz for the centre-forward position. Gyokers’ future Had Alvarez signed, though, Hatchard believes it would have spelled the end for Gyokeres’ Arsenal career. Hatchard has told Arsenal they ‘need’ Gyokeres, who finished as their top scorer last term Getty He continued: “Viktor, who? Adios. He’d have been off to the Metropolitano, I imagine. That’s the brutality of it, but look, the guy had a decent World Cup with Sweden. “He’s won the Premier League. You can’t take that away from him. He did brilliantly for Sporting. He is what he is. “I think there’s an element of Arsenal not always playing to his strengths, but it’s one of those where you are not going to be able to play Havertz in every game. You’re just not because he’ll break down. “So you need to then think, right, if we’re at home to one of the weaker teams, do we then play Gyokeres in that game and make sure that we’re not running Havertz into the ground? “You’ve got (Mikel) Merino as an option as well. So I feel for him a little bit because I think he’s probably not far off what he can do, but I think they haven’t quite adapted to the kind of service he needs.” Gyokeres was an unused substitute against both Coventry City and Aston Villa before featuring off the bench against Chelsea. He also made a brief substitute appearance in the Community Shield win over Manchester City in August. Mikel Arteta’s side continue their Premier League title defence away against Sunderland on Saturday night, live on talkSPORT, kick-off at 8pm.

title_original: Erling Haaland backed to overtake Cristiano Ronaldo and make all-time football history
body_original: Erling Haaland has been tipped to become the highest scorer in football history. The Manchester City striker has already scored five goals in all competitions this season. Haaland has been backed to become football’s all-time leading scorer Getty His latest strikes, a brace against Porto on Tuesday, have seen the 26-year-old tipped to surpass Cristiano Ronaldo’s scoring feats. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner is currently the all-time leading scorer in the history of the sport with 979 goals for club and country. Haaland’s Champions League double has taken his career tally to 364 goals in 440 matches, with Ronaldo having played 890 more times. Haaland backed to become all-time great talkSPORT’s Darren Bent believes the Norway forward can go on to make history, though. Speaking on Drive alongside Andy Goldstein , he admitted: “There’s definitely an argument to say that he could be one of the greatest natural goalscorers we’ve ever seen. His numbers are just crazy.” Bent added: “I know a lot of players that get so bogged down by touches, getting involved and needing to feel it. He does not care if he touches the ball in a game 10 times.” Ronaldo , who turns 42 in February, is set to retire next summer with this season earmarked as his last in professional football. In order to overtake his goal tally, Haaland would have to score 39 goals a season for 16 years if he was to play until he was 42. However, Bent is concerned longevity could be the only factor that stops him from making history. The former England international explained: “The only thing that will stop him being the greatest goalscorer of all-time is longevity. Ronaldo’s record tally currently stands at 973 goals in 1,330 matches for club and country Getty “If he gets injured or something because he has had his injury problems. “I’m not quite sure he’s as durable as (Cristiano) Ronaldo. Ronaldo would just go season upon season upon season.” Haaland has previously faced ankle issues amongst other injuries in his career. His longest absence for City since joining the club in 2022 saw him miss just 10 matches between December 2023 and January 2024, though. Can Haaland surpass Ronaldo? When told how many goals Haaland must score per season to overtake Ronaldo, Bent replied: “There’s no reason why he can’t do that. There’s no reason why he can’t, he’s got everything. “He’s not bothered about touches. All he cares about is that (scoring) and I really respect him. “The biggest compliment I can give him, other than him being fantastic, is that he’s always ready for when that chance comes. “The amount of times a striker will miss an opportunity and we go, ‘he wasn’t ready for that’. That never happens to Haaland. Or we go, ‘that’s come too early for him’. “He almost prides himself on ‘it doesn’t really matter’, minute one or minute 90, whenever it may be, I might not touch the ball for 25 minutes, when that chance comes that’s what I’ve been brought in for. To finish off these chances. “I just think he’s been phenomenal ever since he made his debut.” Haaland’s scoring feats Haaland has already scored 167 goals in 203 appearances for City across the last four years. Of those 115 have been in the Premier League , with Haaland the quickest player ever to reach a century of goals in the competition. Haaland’s brace against Porto has taken his career total to 364 goals in 440 games Getty Erling Haaland's career statistics 2015-17: Bryne – 0 goals in 16 apps 2017-19: Molde – 20 goals in 50 apps 2019-20: Red Bull Salzburg – 29 goals in 27 apps 2020-22: Borussia Dortmund – 86 goals in 89 apps 2022-Present: Manchester City – 167 goals in 203 apps 2019-Present: Norway – 55 goals in 62 caps Total: 364 goals in 440 apps The three-time golden boot also has a goal-a-game record in the Champions League with 59 in 59 for City, Borussia Dortmund and Red Bull Salzburg. His scoring figures at international level are even more impressive, though. Haaland has 62 goals in 55 caps for Norway since making his debut as a 19-year-old in 2019. Those include seven goals at this summer’s World Cup as he fired his nation to the quarter-finals.

title_original: Evangelos Marinakis axes another manager as multi-club owner acts after seven games
body_original: Evangelos Marinakis has sacked Olympiacos manager Jose Luis Mendilibar just seven matches into the new season. The departing boss becomes the 25th manager dismissed by the Greek businessman, who also owns Nottingham Forest and Rio Ave, in 16 years. Mendilibar has been sacked by Olympiacos seven matches into the new season Getty Mendilibar has been dismissed despite not losing a match inside 90 minutes so far this season. However, he has paid the price for Olympiacos’ failure to reach the league phase of the Champions League. His side were beaten on aggregate by NEC in the third qualifying round after an extra-time defeat in the second leg. Despite an unbeaten start domestically in the league and cup, Mendilibar was sacked after Tuesday’s 3-2 win over Volos. Imanol Alguacil has been appointed as the new Olympiacos manager. The former Real Sociedad boss was available after leaving Al Shabab in February. Alguacil previously won the Copa del Rey during his time with Sociedad. His first match in charge of Olympiacos will be at home to OFI Crete on Saturday. Olympiacos statement In a statement confirming his exit, Olympiacos said: “In football, as in life, there are cycles that eventually close, but what resonates in eternity is what you have achieved. “The appreciation, respect and love of the Olympiacos family will accompany you forever, General, along with the strong emotions that united us and are eternal. Thank you for everything.” Mendilibar paid the price for Olympiacos’ early Champions League exit Getty Mendilibar had been in charge since February 2024, with the Spaniard winning the Conference League later that year. He followed up that success with a domestic double in his first full season as manager. Olympiacos missed out on the title last season, though, finishing six points behind AEK Athens. Marinakis’ manager history Mendilibar is the latest manager to be dismissed by Marinakis during his time as a football club owner. The 59-year-old has now axed 25 across his three teams since first buying Olympiacos in 2010. Marinakis completed a takeover of Nottingham Forest in 2017 before adding Portuguese side Rio Ave to his portfolio three years ago. Marinakis has now dismissed 25 managers in 16 years as a football club owner Getty At Forest alone, he had four different permanent managers last season, with Oliver Glasner becoming the club’s fifth head coach in 10 months in July. However, his methods have delivered success across his clubs. Olympiacos have won 11 league titles in 16 years under his stewardship, with Marinakis is into his second spell as club president. Meanwhile, Forest returned to the Premier League for the first time in 23 years back in 2022. They have since remained in the top-flight as well as reaching the Europa League semi-finals last term. As for Rio Ave, they have established themselves in the Liga Portugal, with this season their fifth consecutive campaign in the first-tier.

title_original: Manchester United vs Sabah LIVE commentary: Red Devils handed unique date for Champions League opener
body_original: Manchester United make their long-awaited Champions League return with an unusual Thursday night clash this evening. The Red Devils are appearing in UEFA’s premier club competition for the first time since 2023. United begin their Champions League campaign against Sabah on Thursday night Getty It follows their third place finish in the Premier League last term, having failed to qualify for Europe at all the season prior. Michael Carrick’s side kick-off their league phase campaign at home to Azeri champions Sabah. The match has been scheduled for Thursday night, a rarity in the Champions League . Fixtures are typically played on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, with Thursdays reserved for the Europa League and Conference League. However, matchday one of the Champions League sees matches spread across three dates, with neither of the other competitions starting this week. As a result, United’s is one of six matches being played on Thursday. How to follow Man United vs Sabah The Red Devils welcome Sabah to Old Trafford tonight – Thursday, September 10. Kick-off is scheduled for 8pm, with live commentary available on talkSPORT. Natalie Sawyer will present coverage of the match from 7pm with commentary from Sam Matterface and former Manchester United assistant manager Mike Phelan. Carrick’s side face a rare Champions League outing on a Thursday for their opening fixture Getty Champions League Matchday 1 fixtures Tuesday 8th September AEK Athens 1-0 LASK Club Brugge 2-3 Aston Villa Borussia Dortmund 3-2 Villarreal Lille 2-3 Real Betis Porto 0-2 Manchester City Real Madrid 2-1 Inter Milan Wednesday 9th September Barcelona 5-1 Feyenoord Stuttgart 3-1 Viking Liverpool 2-1 Atletico Madrid Napoli 0-1 Arsenal Paris Saint-Germain 6-1 Slovan Bratislava Sporting CP 3-1 Galatasaray Thursday 10th September Fenerbahce v Roma – 17:45 PSV v Shakhtar Donetsk – 17:45 Bayern Munich v Bodo/Glimt – 20:00 Como v RB Leipzig – 20:00 Manchester United v Sabah – 20:00 – LIVE on talkSPORT Slavia Prague v Lens – 20:00 Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM. Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus. Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, follow us on talkSPORT Facebook and talkSPORT on X . For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET. Man United vs Sabah team news Carrick remains without Carlos Baleba , Matthijs de Ligt and Amad Diallo through injury. The trio are expected to be sidelined until after the international break. Marcus Rashford is also a doubt for the visit of Sabah after he was forced off against Everton on Sunday. Although Carrick revealed post-match it was only a minor issue, the forward is being assessed ahead of Thursday’s match. Manuel Ugarte remains unavailable following knee ligament surgery in the summer. Sabah are competing in the league phase of a UEFA competition for the first time Getty Man United Champions League fixtures September 10 – Sabah (H) October 13 – Atletico Madrid (A) October 21 – Como (A) November 3 – Roma (H) November 25 – Sporting Lisbon (A) December 12 – RB Leipzig (H) January 20 – Bayern Munich (H) January 27 – Villarreal (A) Who are Sabah? This week’s match represents United’s first-ever competitive meeting with a club from Azerbaijan. Sabah are also playing in the group stage or league phase of a European competition for the first time. Founded in 2017, the won their maiden league title as part of a league and cup double last season. Wins over The New Saints, KuPS, Aarhus and Hapoel Be’er Sheva have seen them into the league phase. The club are based in the town of Masazir in eastern Azerbaijan, which has a population of just under 19,000. As a result, the population of the town could fit into Old Trafford almost four times over.

title_original: Mauricio Pochettino branded a ‘loser’ for saying Tottenham should get Chelsea’s 2017 title
body_original: Mauricio Pochettino has been called out for a ‘loser mentality’ after claiming Tottenham deserve to be awarded Chelsea’s 2016/17 Premier League title. The Argentine’s Spurs side finished runner-up to Antonio Conte ‘s Blues that season, seven points adrift of the eventual champions. Conte won the Premier League and FA Cup during his two-year spell in charge of Chelsea between 2016-2018 Getty However, Pochettino believes Chelsea should be stripped of the trophy, having admitted to breaking the rules. The current Blues administration self-reported widespread financial irregularities that occurred during the Roman Abramovich era. This included millions in secret payments to agents, helping to secure a number of players that starred in the 2016/17 title-winning season – including Eden Hazard , Willian and David Luiz. Chelsea escaped with a £10million fine and a suspended transfer ban, avoiding any sporting sanctions . But Pochettino, who also managed the Blues in recent years, argues the 2016/17 title should be retrospectively given to his Tottenham side by default. “I have no doubt and I’m not scared to say the truth,” the current USA manager said. “The Chelsea fans will be upset with me because I’m saying this. “It’s not me complaining. It’s the truth. “If they admitted they broke the rules, the Premier League title was for the second best team. “Otherwise, what is being promoted and incentivised is to break the rules. They admitted, so that’s it. The title should be for the team that was second.” Hazard was the best player in the Premier League during the 2016/17 season Getty But should it have been Harry Kane lifting the trophy? Pochettino added: “If we were at Tottenham and broke the rules I’d admit the same and say ‘look, we don’t deserve the title because we broke the rules’. “You don’t have some clubs playing with the offside laws and VAR and another side without them. That’s impossible. “No. For everyone it needs to be the same rules and the same capacity to create the best team. “I’m not saying they didn’t play well. “That was Conte, the coach was great, and everything.” ‘Loser mentality’ talkSPORT pundit and Chelsea fan Rory Jennings ripped into Pochettino for his outlandish claim on Wednesday night’s Sports Bar. Pochettino’s men came up seven points short in the 2016/17 season and never truly threatened Chelsea for the title AFP or licensors “Pochettino is demonstrating loser mentality,” Jennings told co-host and Tottenham fan Majestic. “That’s what this is. “Give us something on a technicality that we didn’t really earn. You don’t want that. You’re better than this.” Veteran talkSPORT host and former Tottenham striker Alan Brazil also dismissed Pochettino’s calls for the record to be rewritten. “It doesn’t work like that. It’s gone now,” Brazil said on Thursday morning’s Breakfast Show.

title_original: Andoni Iraola gives update on Bradley Barcola injury as Liverpool fans hold breath on £123m man
body_original: Andoni Iraola has assured Liverpool fans that Bradley Barcola coming off during their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid was just a bout of cramp. The French winger, who joined the Reds for an initial £106million rising to £123m this summer, went down just before the hour mark in the Champions League clash at Anfield on Wednesday night. Barcola’s issue is not as bad as first feared TNT Sports Barcola appeared in some discomfort and rubbed his left calf while receiving medical treatment. He was then substituted, with Jeremie Frimpong coming on in his place. Andoni Iraola provides update on Bradley Barcola injury However, in a major boost, Reds boss Iraola insisted there was no serious issue with Barcola. “It’s just cramps, especially with Bradley,” Iraola said. “We are kind of rushing him as we haven’t had him in pre-season.” The Champions League fixture marked Barcola’s first start for Liverpool, having made his Premier League debut courtesy of a 26-minute cameo off the bench last Friday against Ipswich Town. Barcola’s injury came just minutes after he missed a golden chance to put Liverpool in the lead. The French flyer was slipped in via a perfect through-ball from Florian Wirtz and raced clear towards goal, but he fired his effort wide of the post. Luckily for Barcola, Alexis Mac Allister would not have such worries just minutes later. The midfielder, who recently confirmed Liverpool did not intend to offer him a new contract , let rip with a thunderous left-footed strike from just outside the box to put the hosts in the lead. Llorente has proved to be a constant thorn in Liverpool’s side Getty But Mac Allister ensured it would be a winning start in Europe for Liverpool Getty Marcos Llorente opened the scoring in the 17th minute when he ghosted past Milos Kerkez and fizzed a driven effort past Alisson. It was the tenth goal of Llorente’s career in the competition. Remarkably, five of those have been scored against Liverpool, all of which have come at Anfield. It took Liverpool until the 40th minute to equalise, with Dominik Szoboszlai the man to bring the scores level. However, most of the plaudits for the equaliser went to Ronald Araujo as he nutmegged an Atleti defender with a deft flick that went straight to Szoboszlai, who then stroked the ball past Jan Oblak. Frimpong then thought he doubled Liverpool’s advantage just before second-half stoppage time when he scored on the rebound from close range. However, it was immediately ruled out for offside, with replays confirming the on-field decision. Liverpool’s next outing sees them entertain Fulham on Saturday with their next Champions League game away at Austrian side LASK on October 14.

title_original: Michael Carrick’s brother handed new England coaching role
body_original: Michael Carrick’s younger brother, Graeme, has been appointed as an assistant coach of the England Under-17 side. The FA revealed their full coaching list for all of the Young Lions sides on Wednesday, confirming the set-ups. Graeme has secured a first coaching role since working alongside his brother Michael at Middlesbrough Carrick will be working under manager Barry Lewtas and alongside Matt Thorpe and Matt Doyle with the Under-17s. His role comes at an important time, as England’s youth team begin their bid for glory at the 2027 European Under-17 Championship. Qualifiers are set to kick off in November ahead of the tournament finals in Latvia next summer. In his new coaching role, Carrick will oversee the development of the country’s most promising talents, as he looks to guide them in their goal to one day represent Thomas Tuchel ‘s senior side. And he could soon be working with some future stars, with the most recent England Under-17s squad featuring Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel and Chelsea starlet Ryan Kavuma-McQueen. Carrick’s appointment wasn’t the only eye-catching name in the England youth teams’ coaching announcements. Ex-Wolves and Leicester defender Conor Coady was confirmed as one of the England’s Under-21s assistant managers , just days after his departure as a player from Wrexham . Meanwhile, former Premier League boss Darren Moore has been named as the new manager of the England Under-20 side . Former Man United, Tottenham and Hull midfielder Tom Huddlestone is also part of the backroom team with the Under-19s. Graeme Carrick’s coaching career Graeme’s new position in the England youth set-up sees him return to coaching after a year out of the game. Graeme has previous experience elite youth coaching experience at Newcastle Getty Graeme lined up alongside brother Michael in his 2017 testimonial match Getty His last role was assistant to his brother Michael at Middlesbrough , where he joined the current Man United boss for the final year of his three-year stint on Teeside. Graeme’s football career was cut short by injuries as a youngster while Michael went on to star for the likes of Tottenham, the Red Devils and England. Instead, the younger Carrick brother pursued a coaching career, and worked with Newcastle’s youth teams and the FA’s elite youth development sides. In 2022, Graeme returned to the Magpies to take charge of their Under-18s, before he moved into the senior game. He joined Michael at Middlesbrough in 2024, and served as his brother’s assistant for 49 games. However, the pair both departed in June 2025 following Michael’s sacking as head coach . Michael was confirmed as Man United’s permanent boss in May after impressing in interim charge Getty While Graeme embarks on his role with England, his brother is looking to build on his growing reputation at Man United following his permanent appointment in the summer. After guiding his team to a third-place finish last season, Carrick’s side make their Champions League return on Thursday night. The Red Devils kick-off their league phase campaign at home to Azerbaijan champions Sabah , with live commentary on talkSPORT. Carrick will be juggling European competition with United’s Premeri League ambitions this term, where his side have picked just four points from their first three games.

title_original: Newcastle tipped to sell Lewis Hall despite new contract amid worrying comments from sporting director
body_original: Newcastle selling Lewis Hall next summer has not been completely ruled out. Hall is understood to have signed a new contract committing his future to the Magpies until 2031. Hall’s new contract will run until 2031 Getty The left-back was a target for Manchester United this summer and he was believed to be open to a move. United were told he was not for sale , regardless of what they offered. Now Hall is expected to become one of the best-paid players at St James’ Park, in recognition of his importance for new manager Matthias Jaissle. Inside Lewis Hall’s contract extension talkSPORT reporter Ben Jacobs said: “It’s a five-year contract that adds two years to the existing deal. So it keeps Hall at the club until 2031. “There were always these two extremes at play. Either Manchester United would make an approach, would have to overpay, and Hall would have been somewhat open to that move. “Or he stays and under the new manager, Matthias Jaissle, is invested in the project, and then he signs a new deal. “But it was never just going to continue with Hall staying and not being offered improved terms. “Newcastle have been able to keep Hall because he was never unhappy with Newcastle the club, only unhappy with how last season ended, where he was in and out of the side. “He lost his England place. Dan Burn, his Newcastle teammate, got picked in his place. “All of that led Hall to, in the early part of the summer, at least put the brakes on signing because the nuts and bolts of this deal were in place in February or March. Jaissle emphatically ruled out a summer move for Hall Getty “Then Eddie Howe leaves, Matthias Jaissle comes in. He’s had a very positive effect on all players, including Lewis Hall. And Jaissle has told Hall he is integral, he is the number one left-back. “Then from there, there was no hesitation in getting this deal over the line. “Of course, we have to say with Morgan Rogers , he extended late last year. He still left the following summer. “So I don’t think we can say categorically, depending on how the season goes, that Hall is unavailable in the summer 2027 market. “But it’s a really positive sign for Newcastle. If everything now goes according to plan, then Hall will remain invested in this project.” Newcastle’s summer overhaul It has been a summer of upheaval for Newcastle having brought in £244million by selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes. Gordon was one of three key players sold by Newcastle this summer Getty Sporting director Ross Wilson has hinted this could continue in the years ahead. “If you want to be a successful club in the Premier League , you have to trade players and if you don’t the chances are you won’t be a successful club in the Premier League,” Wilson said. “This is what we’ve got to do. And if you don’t do it, then just keep the squad you’ve got and forevermore they’ll grow old, achieve less and leave for nothing.” Former Crystal Palace owner Simon Jordan believes Newcastle will never get to their aim of being a Premier League winning club if they maintain this course of action. Jordan: “If you want to be a club that’s winning the Premier League, then you’ve got to do two things. You’ve got to keep your best players and you’ve got to massively, massively increase the revenue of this football club. “If you’re going to compete with Manchester City, Liverpool, Arsenal, even Tottenham, irrespective of whether Tottenham’s form on the field at the moment is dreadful, you have got to get your turnover up by double what you’ve got now.” He added: “They sold Tonali, Guimaraes, and Isak. “They’ll keep him (Hall) until someone else comes along and decides they’re going to take him. “By the admission of their sporting director, they will continue to sell players to comply with PSR because the rules of PSR are so patently unfair for teams like Newcastle.”

title_original: La Federación pasa de Marruecos: «Es un movimiento político, la final la tenemos que hacer nosotros»
body_original: La Real Federación Española de Fútbol mantiene la calma pese a las palabras del ministro de Presupuesto marroquí y presidente de su federación de fútbol, Fouzi Lekjaa, que ha afirmado que «Casablanca tendrá el honor de organizar la final del Mundial de 2030». Siguen apostando por Madrid como la gran candi target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">la FIFA aún no ha decidido nada, como han vuelto a acreditar este jueves. Algo que ya hicieron el pasado 5 de agosto, cuando, tras el Congreso de la FIFA celebrado en Marruecos, se filtró que el presidente del máximo organismo futbolístico prometió la final al país si, de esa forma, se garantizaba el apoyo de la Confederación de África. Salieron a desmentirlo desde Zúrich, dejando claro que «la FIFA tomará una decisión a su debido tiempo». A eso mismo se remiten desde la RFEF. La FIFA deberá aún hacer una última visita a los tres países organizadores (España, Portugal y Marruecos) antes de dar un resultado final sobre las sedes de ese Mundial y en ese momento seguirá sin haberse decidido la ciudad que albergará la final. Se daba por hecho que sería en Madrid, aunque en los últimos tiempos las presiones de todo tipo de Marruecos lo han puesto en duda. Donde no las tienen es en la Federación. La confianza en que la final sea en España es absoluta. Sobre todo, tras la consecución del Mundial 2026 en Estados Unidos. La consecución de la Copa del Mundo por parte de los hombres de Luis de la Fuente fue un impulso que debería ser definitivo . aunque Marruecos no se da por vencido. A la espera de Valencia y Vigo Aunque Marruecos, en boca del presidente de su federación –que a su vez es ministro del Gobierno– ha afirmado que la final será en Casablanca. Sin embargo, hoy por hoy no están elegidas ni las sedes definitivas. España todavía no sabe con cuántas contará, aunque tienen claro que quieren que sean 11, incluyendo a Vigo y Valencia , que están en duda. Para ello, es necesario que la delegación de FIFA acuda a ver cómo evolucionan las obras del Nou Mestalla y que lo hagan también al estadio del Celta, Balaídos, también inmerso en una importantísima reestructuración. La candidatura de España quiere que ambas ciudades sean incluidas entre las sedes finales para el Mundial 2030 y, de momento, la RFEF ha hecho lo que toca, que es solicitar a la FIFA que acuda a ambas ciudades en su próxima y definitiva visita.

title_original: ‘Amazing story’ – How Loris Karius bounced back from night that almost ended his career
body_original: Loris Karius’ nightmare 2018 Champions League final could have spelt the end of his top-level career. The then- Liverpool goalkeeper – who it later transpired had been concussed earlier in the game – was at fault for two of the goals the Reds conceded in a 3-1 defeat to Real Madrid in Kyiv, receiving death threats after the game. Karius is now first choice between the sticks for Miron Muslic’s Schalke Getty Karius never played for Liverpool again, but the 33-year-old has gone on to revive his career and is currently impressing for Schalke in his native Germany, helping them win promotion back to the Bundesliga as second-tier champions last season. ‘An amazing story’ And it’s ‘amazing’ to see him back at the highest level, says European football expert Andy Brassell. He told talkSPORT: “What happened in Kyiv in 2018 is something that would have finished most players – and it almost did finish him. “It blew his career off course for ages. A load of his peak disappeared while he was flitting between clubs and out of teams. “You look at: running aground at Besiktas because they weren’t paying him, then you had being a reserve at [Hertha] Berlin, being an emergency third choice at Newcastle , and then ending up in the second tier at Schalke. It’s an amazing story for him to get back to where he is, really.” Karius keeps Kane out (again) Karius produced a sensational save to deny Ballon d’Or frontrunner Harry Kane late on as Schalke held reigning German champions Bayern Munich to a 0-0 draw last time out. In doing so, he became the first ‘keeper to keep a Bundesliga clean sheet against Bayern for almost 18 months. Matej Kovar of Bayer Leverkusen was the last do so towards the end of the 2024/25 campaign. In that point-securing moment, it felt like Karius’ career had come full circle, with Brassell alluding to a penalty he saved from Kane while playing for Liverpool a few months before the 2018 Champions League final. “When he saved that penalty from Kane, I guess people thought he could still develop into one of the better players in the Premier League ,” Brassell continued. “He’d already had that little spell at Manchester City with the [Under] 18s and 21s, which is how he knew [current Bayern boss and former Man City captain] Vincent Kompany . Kompany congratulated him personally at the end of this game [for Schalke against Bayern]. Karius made five saves to deny Bayern on Saturday Getty “At that point when he was at Liverpool, you thought he was going to develop into one of the key goalkeepers in the Premier League. Then Kyiv and everything else happened.” Karius on ‘great’ day Eight years later, Karius looks to be in a good place, cementing his spot as Schalke’s No.1 in the top flight, with Brassell noting: “[He’s] got past setbacks that would definitely end the careers or top-level careers of most players. “For him to arrive back at this point at 33 and be able to do this is amazing.” Speaking after his heroic display at the weekend, Karius said: “It was great for me. I only had to shout to keep going, move up, drop back. “Real credit to the guys for what they did. They kept so much away and made things so incredibly hard for Bayern. The guys really worked hard until they couldn’t go anymore. Everyone today can be proud of their performance.” He also drew praise from his opposite number, goalkeeping legend and Schalke academy graduate Manuel Neuer , who said: “Loris Karius was very good and definitely the right choice for man of the match. “We had three big chances that he kept out. That was definitely key to us not winning this game.”

title_original: Harry Kane joins elite Champions League group with Cristiano Ronaldo as Bayern Munich add to stunning run
body_original: Harry Kane scored in an eighth consecutive Champions League match as Bayern Munich beat Bodo/Glimt 5-0 in their league phase opener. After assisting Jamal Musiala early on in the second half, Kane bagged their second of the night with a close-range header on 61 minutes. Kane doubled the lead for Bayern as they thumped Bodo/Glimt Getty The goal was his 55th in the Champions League and came on his 71st competition outing. However, more impressively, Kane has become one of four players to score in eight or more consecutive matches in the competition. He has followed Cristiano Ronaldo and Robert Lewandowski, who did so on two occasions each, as well as Ruud van Nistelrooy. Kane goals in last eight Champions League matches September 10 – One goal vs Bodo/Glimt – League phase May 6 – One goal vs Paris Saint-Germain – Semi-final second leg April 28 – One goal vs Paris Saint-Germain – Semi-final first leg April 15 – One goal vs Real Madrid – Quarter-final second leg April 7 – One goal vs Real Madrid – Quarter-final first leg March 18 – Two goals vs Atalanta – Last 16 second leg January 28 – One goal vs PSV Eindhoven – League phase January 21 – Two goals vs Royale Union Saint-Gilloise – League phase Bayern have won their opening match in the Champions League for a 23rd straight season, scoring 68 goals and conceding only eight. Alphonso Davies scored their third of the night before a double from Michael Olise wrapped it up late on. Bodo/Glimt went down to ten men with three minutes remaining in normal time when Odin Bjortuft saw red for a last-man foul. How many goals has Kane scored this season? After netting 61 times in all competitions last season, Kane has had a relatively slow start by his impressive standards. The England captain scored on his third appearance of the campaign when Bayern beat VfL Osnabruck 4-1 in the DFB-Pokal. Kane’s header against Bodo/Glimt has taken him to three goals in five matches for 2026/27 thus far. All that’s missing is a goal in the Bundesliga, in which he was the top scorer during the previous campaign with 36. Kane has found the back of the net in eight straight Champions League matches Getty He has joined Ronaldo, as well as Lewandowski and Van Nistelrooy in the elite group Getty He played that majority of the 5-1 win over Stuttgart, but was a surprise substitute in the 0-0 draw with Schalke. Kane is now on a whopping total of 149 goals for Bayern, and could be heading towards Ballon d’Or glory. The 33-year-old is one of 30 nominees for this year’s award and a favourite to win football’s most prestigious individual prize. Who do Bayern play in the Champions League? Norwegian side Viking FK host six-time winners Bayern in the next stage of the league phase on October 13. Back-to-back tests against Arsenal and Atletico Madrid follow, with Lille and Slavia Prague their last two opponents in 2026. At the beginning of 2027, it’s Manchester United and Real Betis who complete their league phase schedule.

title_original: Hakim Ziyech finds new club four days after ex-Chelsea star had contract terminated
body_original: Former Chelsea forward Hakim Ziyech has signed for Brazilian giants Botafogo on a free transfer. Ziyech had only been without a club since Sunday, when his contract with Moroccan club Wydad was terminated. Ex-Chelsea star Ziyech has signed for Botafogo days after terminating his contract Getty The 33-year-old winger departed after 11 months, having played 16 games and scored nine goals, assisting two. But he has now made an instant move to Brazil, signing a two-year deal with Botafogo on Thursday. Botafogo officially announced the move on social media, writing: “Hakim Ziyech is with BOTAFOGO. “World Cup player and multi-champion in Europe, the attacking midfielder signs with the Glorious One until the end of 2028.” Why did Hakim Ziyech leave Wydad? Ziyech, who won the Champions League with Chelsea in 2021, received thanks from Wydad after leaving the club. A mutual agreement was reached to rip up his contract, seemingly to allow him to make a move elsewhere for free. Wydad wrote: “Sometimes, some stories are shorter than we had hoped, but they leave a mark that cannot be erased. “You were one of us, and you will always remain part of the Wydad Athletic family. “From the Wydad of the nation, we say thank you for every moment in which you wore the club’s shirt, and we wish you every success and good fortune in your coming career, on the pitch and off it. “Some journeys may come to an end, but the memories remain, and Wydad will always have a place in your heart. Thank you, Hakim, for being part of our story.” Ziyech has played for Galatasaray, Al-Duhail and Wydad since leaving Chelsea in 2023 Getty Who else plays for Botafogo? Ziyech, who chipped in with six goals and nine assists from 34 English top-flight matches between 2020-2023, will now be playing alongside some fellow former Premier League stars. Ex- Manchester United defender Alex Telles, former Everton midfielder Allan and ex- Nottingham Forest star Danilo are all part of the squad that the Moroccan has joined. Jesse Lingard is also playing in the Brazilian Serie A with Corinthians, while Jadon Sancho has been linked with the league too. Ziyech’s old Chelsea teammate Thiago Silva , Andreas Pereira and Memphis Depay are just some of the other former Premier League players competing in the division. And of course, Brazil icon Neymar still plays in his home nation. Ziyech could make his Botafogo debut against RB Bragantino on Saturday, with kick-off at midnight in the UK.

title_original: ‘He’s struggling’ – Liverpool starter must step up or risk brutal transfer
body_original: Milos Kerkez must up his game at Liverpool or risk being sold – he is not justifying his £40million price tag. That’s the view of many across the talkSPORT network as the 22-year-old continues to struggle since joining the Reds from Bournemouth in 2025 . Liverpool defender Kerkez is struggling for form, leading many to question his role in the team Getty A stellar 2024/25 season at the Vitality Stadium saw the left-back register eight goal contributions from 38 top-flight matches. But he failed to replicate the form that saw him emerge as one of the division’s top full-backs in his opening campaign in Merseyside. Chipping in with just one goal and two assists, the defensive part of his game was also called into question. There was hope from Reds fans that his performances would improve this term after his former mentor Andoni Iraola replaced Arne Slot in the dugout. However, despite starting in the club’s opening four games of the season, his struggles persist, with his ball-watching almost proving costly in Wednesday night’s 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in the Champions League. He allowed Marcos Llorente to run beyond him after failing in his attempt to play the offside trap, with Liverpool managing to fight back to claim all three points. What has been said about Milos Kerkez? Prior to the game, Liverpool cult hero Danny Murphy told talkSPORT that the player is one of Iraola’s biggest problems . And now legendary broadcaster Andy Gray, who was on commentary duty for talkSPORT , has cast doubts over Kerkez . He said: “The Kerkez I saw at Bournemouth is not the Kerkez I am watching right now, that’s what I would say. “I was not surprised Liverpool went and bought him when he was playing for Bournemouth – one of the best full-backs in the league by a distance. Hungary international Kerkez has failed to replicate the form he showed at Bournemouth AFP “But he hasn’t quite settled into that role where he was there. “I don’t know whether sometimes a club’s too big for people, I hope that’s not the case with Kerkez.” Kerkez was a topic of discussion on the Sports Breakfast show on Thursday morning, with Rangers legend Ally McCoist quick to point out his role in Atletico’s opener. He stated: “He’s struggling, isn’t he? You can see it, and it’s not through lack of effort, he’s definitely trying to get forward, but he gets caught for the goal. “I don’t know what he’s thinking about the goal, he’s got to look at the ball and see that he’s not going to get out in time. “He’s deeper than his two centre-backs, Llorente has timed his run well and finishes it really, really well.” Kerkez still has four years left on his contract in Merseyside AFP Meanwhile, the Telegraph’s Merseyside correspondent Dom King questioned whether Liverpool could look to sell Kerkez should his form not improve. He remarked: “There is a position that either Milos Kerkez has to raise the standards or it will end up being something that Liverpool have to assess. “But still a work in progress, when they don’t press in sync then there’s problems for the defence, but they’re getting there.” For ex-Manchester United forward Alan Brazil, his mind has already been made up over the defender – insisting Liverpool should bin him off in 2027. In a blunt assessment of Kerkez, he simply stated: “He’s got to go, I’m sorry.” Charlie Adam, who won the League Cup at Liverpool in 2012, was yet another that has commented on growing concerns regarding Kerkez. Iraola is yet to taste defeat from his opening four matches as Liverpool boss Getty He said: “I thought there were moments [against Atletico] where I just worry, at times Liverpool are so open, when they go and they try and go full press they’re getting caught at the moment. “A lot of the goals last year were similar to that in transition, there were big spaces for Atletico to attack and that’s where the goal comes from into [Julian] Alvarez and he slides it in [to Llorente]. “I think the back line, Kerkez needs to drop because [Virgil] van Dijk actually pushes up and he doesn’t see what’s behind him, Kerkez needs to go with the runner.” It remains to be seen whether Kerkez will start against Fulham on Saturday, or whether Iraola turns to Kostas Tsimikas.
